Its point update is proved like sum's, by induction through steps with no quantifier.

The sum of basin b's cells among xs.[0 .. n].

let spec bsum (xs : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (n : usize) : u64
  requires n <= len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  reads xs.[c] where label.[c] = b
  ensures result <= (max u32 + 1) * n
  decreases n
= if n = 0 then 0 else bsum xs label b (n - 1) + (if label.[n - 1] = b then elt xs (n - 1) else 0)

let lemma bstep (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires 0 < n && n <= len xs && len ys = len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires bsum ys label b (n - 1) = bsum xs label b (n - 1) && ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]
  ensures bsum ys label b n = bsum xs label b n
= ()

let lemma bstep_after (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (i : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires i < n - 1 && n <= len xs && len ys = len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires bsum ys label b (n - 1) + xs.[i] = bsum xs label b (n - 1) + ys.[i] && ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]
  ensures bsum ys label b n + xs.[i] = bsum xs label b n + ys.[i]
= ()

let lemma bstep_at (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (i : usize) : unit
  requires i < len xs && len ys = len xs && len label = len xs && i < max u32 + 1 && label.[i] = b
  requires bsum ys label b i = bsum xs label b i
  ensures bsum ys label b (i + 1) + xs.[i] = bsum xs label b (i + 1) + ys.[i]
= ()

let lemma bframe (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (i : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires len ys = len xs && len label = len xs && n <= i && i < len xs && len xs <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len xs). k <> i ==> ys.[k] = xs.[k]
  ensures bsum ys label b n = bsum xs label b n
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then (bframe xs ys label b i (n - 1); assert ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]; bstep xs ys label b n)

The point update for a cell of basin b.

let lemma bupdate (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (i : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires len ys = len xs && len label = len xs && i < n && n <= len xs && len xs <= max u32 + 1
  requires label.[i] = b
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len xs). k <> i ==> ys.[k] = xs.[k]
  ensures bsum ys label b n + xs.[i] = bsum xs label b n + ys.[i]
  decreases n
= if n > i + 1 then (bupdate xs ys label b i (n - 1); assert ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]; bstep_after xs ys label b i n)
  else (bframe xs ys label b i i; bstep_at xs ys label b i; assert n = i + 1)

let lemma bat_le (xs : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (i : usize) : unit
  requires i < len xs && len label = len xs && i < max u32 + 1 && label.[i] = b
  ensures xs.[i] <= bsum xs label b (i + 1)
= ()

let lemma bmono (xs : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (m : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires m <= n && n <= len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  ensures bsum xs label b m <= bsum xs label b n
  decreases n
= if n > m then bmono xs label b m (n - 1)

A cell of basin b is at most the basin's sum.

let lemma belt_le (xs : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (i : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires i < n && n <= len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1 && label.[i] = b
  ensures xs.[i] <= bsum xs label b n
= bat_le xs label b i; bmono xs label b (i + 1) n

A write to a cell of basin b, whose contract is the point update for the basin's sum; it touches only that cell.

let bset (xs : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (i : usize) (v : u32) : unit @owns(xs, label, b)
  requires i < len xs && len label = len xs && len xs <= max u32 + 1 && label.[i] = b
  ensures xs.[i] = v
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len xs). k <> i ==> xs.[k] = old (xs.[k])
  ensures bsum xs label b (len xs) + old (xs.[i]) = bsum (old xs) label b (len xs) + v
= let w = xs.[i] in
  xs.[i] <- v;
  bupdate (old xs) xs label b i (len xs);
  assert w = old (xs.[i])

docs.title: 4. A step in one basin
docs.text:
The functions of a time step, each with a footprint: @owns(bed, label, bas) says it touches only the cells of basin bas, so a spread over basins may call it for its own basin (ADR 0060). Each conserves the basin's total.

The load of cell a moves into the inflow of cell b, both in basin bas.

let bpush (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (label : [usize]) (bas : usize) (a : usize) (b : usize) : unit @owns(load, label, bas) @owns(inflow, label, bas)
  requires a < len load && b < len inflow && len load <= max u32 + 1 && len inflow = len load && len label = len load
  requires label.[a] = bas && label.[b] = bas
  requires bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) <= max u32
  ensures load.[a] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> a ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) = bsum (old load) label bas (len load) + bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow)
= let m = load.[a] in
  let w = inflow.[b] in
  belt_le load label bas a (len load);
  belt_le inflow label bas b (len inflow);
  bset load label bas a 0;
  bset inflow label bas b (w + m)

The load of an outlet of basin bas leaves the map.

let bdrain (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (label : [usize]) (bas : usize) (a : usize) (gone : u64) : u64 @owns(load, label, bas)
  requires a < len load && len load <= max u32 + 1 && len label = len load && label.[a] = bas
  requires bsum load label bas (len load) + gone <= max u32
  ensures load.[a] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> a ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures bsum load label bas (len load) + result = bsum (old load) label bas (len load) + gone
= let m = load.[a] in
  belt_le load label bas a (len load);
  bset load label bas a 0;
  gone + m

A cell of basin bas takes its inflow and erodes or deposits.

let berode (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (label : [usize]) (bas : usize) (c : usize) (capacity : u32) : unit @owns(bed, label, bas) @owns(load, label, bas) @owns(inflow, label, bas)
  requires c < len bed && len load = len bed && len inflow = len bed && len label = len bed
  requires len bed <= max u32 + 1 && label.[c] = bas
  requires bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) <= max u32
  requires load.[c] = 0
  ensures inflow.[c] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> c ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) =
    bsum (old bed) label bas (len bed) + bsum (old load) label bas (len load) + bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow)
= let i = inflow.[c] in
  let d = bed.[c] in
  belt_le bed label bas c (len bed);
  belt_le inflow label bas c (len inflow);
  let r = erode_or_deposit i capacity d in
  bset bed label bas c r.bed;
  assert bsum bed label bas (len bed) + d = bsum (old bed) label bas (len bed) + r.bed;
  bset load label bas c r.load;
  assert bsum load label bas (len load) = bsum (old load) label bas (len load) + r.load;
  bset inflow label bas c 0;
  assert bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) + i = bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow);
  balance (bsum bed label bas (len bed)) (bsum load label bas (len load)) (bsum inflow label bas (len inflow))
    (bsum (old bed) label bas (len bed)) (bsum (old load) label bas (len load)) (bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow))
    d i r.bed r.load

One transfer within basin bas.

let btransfer (bed : [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (label : [usize]) (bas : usize) (a : usize) (b : usize) (outlet : bool) (gone : u64) : u64 @owns(bed, label, bas) @owns(load, label, bas) @owns(inflow, label, bas)
  requires a < len load && b < len inflow && len bed = len load && len inflow = len load && len label = len load
  requires len load <= max u32 + 1 && label.[a] = bas && label.[b] = bas
  requires bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) + gone <= max u32
  ensures load.[a] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> a ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) + result =
    bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum (old load) label bas (len load) + bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow) + gone
= if outlet then bdrain load label bas a gone
  else (bpush load inflow label bas a b; gone)

One cell of a step within basin bas.

let bvisit (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (flux : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (label : [usize]) (bas : usize) (c : usize) (d : usize) (capacity : u32) (gone : u64) : u64 @owns(bed, label, bas) @owns(load, label, bas) @owns(inflow, label, bas) @owns(flux, label, bas)
  requires c < len bed && d < len bed && len load = len bed && len inflow = len bed && len flux = len bed && len label = len bed
  requires len bed <= max u32 + 1 && label.[c] = bas && label.[d] = bas
  requires load.[c] = 0
  requires bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) + gone <= max u32
  ensures load.[c] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> c ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) + result =
    bsum (old bed) label bas (len bed) + bsum (old load) label bas (len load) + bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow) + gone
= berode bed load inflow label bas c capacity;
  chain (bsum (old bed) label bas (len bed)) (bsum (old load) label bas (len load)) (bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow)) gone
    (bsum bed label bas (len bed)) (bsum load label bas (len load)) (bsum inflow label bas (len inflow));
  flux.[c] <- load.[c];
  let r = btransfer bed load inflow label bas c d (d = c) gone in
  r

One time step over basin bas: its cells, places lo up to hi of the grouped order, highest first. Conserves the basin's total.

let btransport (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (border : [usize]) (label : [usize]) (bas : usize) (lo : usize) (hi : usize)
    (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (flux : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (gone : u64) : u64
    @owns(bed, label, bas) @owns(load, label, bas) @owns(inflow, label, bas) @owns(flux, label, bas)
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len border = len fill && len label = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len load = len fill && len inflow = len fill && len flux = len fill
  requires len fill <= max u32 + 1 && lo <= hi && hi <= len border
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down).
             down.[k] = k || (down.[k] < len fill && fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len label). label.[at down k] = label.[k]
  requires forall (q in lo .. hi). border.[q] < len fill && label.[border.[q]] = bas
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len load). label.[k] = bas ==> load.[k] = 0
  requires bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) + gone <= max u32
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). label.[k] = bas ==> load.[k] = 0
  ensures bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) + result =
    bsum (old bed) label bas (len bed) + bsum (old load) label bas (len load) + bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow) + gone
=
  let g : mutable u64 = gone in
  for p in lo .. hi
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. len load). label.[k] = bas ==> load.[k] = 0
    invariant bsum bed label bas (len bed) + bsum load label bas (len load) + bsum inflow label bas (len inflow) + g =
      bsum (old bed) label bas (len bed) + bsum (old load) label bas (len load) + bsum (old inflow) label bas (len inflow) + gone
  do
    let c = border.[p] in
    let d = down.[c] in
    assert label.[at down c] = label.[c];
    let drop : u16 = if d = c then 0 else fill.[c] - fill.[d] in
    g <- bvisit bed load inflow flux label bas c d (capacity_of acc.[c] drop) g
  done;
  g

docs.title: 5. Every basin at once
docs.text:
lsum is the sum of the cells whose label is below nb. Splitting off the last basin, and taking every label, show that the basins' sums add up to the whole sum, and lsum_balance adds the per-basin laws up into the law for the map.

The sum of the cells among xs.[0 .. n] whose label is below nb.

let spec lsum (xs : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (nb : usize) (n : usize) : u64
  requires n <= len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  ensures result <= sum xs n
  decreases n
= if n = 0 then 0 else lsum xs label nb (n - 1) + (if label.[n - 1] < nb then elt xs (n - 1) else 0)

Splitting off the last basin: the cells below nb are those below nb - 1 and those of basin nb - 1.

let lemma lsum_split (xs : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (nb : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires 0 < nb && n <= len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  ensures lsum xs label nb n = lsum xs label (nb - 1) n + bsum xs label (nb - 1) n
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then lsum_split xs label nb (n - 1)

When every label is below nb, the cells below nb are all of them.

let lemma lsum_all (xs : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (nb : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires n <= len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. n). at label k < nb
  ensures lsum xs label nb n = sum xs n
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then (lsum_all xs label nb (n - 1); assert at label (n - 1) < nb)

The arithmetic of one basin more.

let lemma add_basin (l1 : u64) (l2 : u64) (l3 : u64) (g : u64) (m1 : u64) (m2 : u64) (m3 : u64)
    (b1 : u64) (b2 : u64) (b3 : u64) (gb : u32) (c1 : u64) (c2 : u64) (c3 : u64)
    (n1 : u64) (n2 : u64) (n3 : u64) (h : u64) (k1 : u64) (k2 : u64) (k3 : u64) : unit
  requires l1 + l2 + l3 + g = m1 + m2 + m3
  requires b1 + b2 + b3 + gb = c1 + c2 + c3
  requires n1 = l1 + b1 && n2 = l2 + b2 && n3 = l3 + b3 && h = g + gb
  requires k1 = m1 + c1 && k2 = m2 + c2 && k3 = m3 + c3
  ensures n1 + n2 + n3 + h = k1 + k2 + k3
= ()

One basin more, without the quantifier.

let lemma balance_step (bed : [u32]) (load : [u32]) (inflow : [u32]) (bed0 : [u32]) (load0 : [u32]) (inflow0 : [u32])
    (gone : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (nb : usize) : unit
  requires len load = len bed && len inflow = len bed && len bed0 = len bed && len load0 = len bed
  requires len inflow0 = len bed && len label = len bed && len bed <= max u32 + 1
  requires 0 < nb && nb <= len gone && len gone <= max u32 + 1
  requires lsum bed label (nb - 1) (len bed) + lsum load label (nb - 1) (len bed) + lsum inflow label (nb - 1) (len bed) + sum gone (nb - 1) =
    lsum bed0 label (nb - 1) (len bed) + lsum load0 label (nb - 1) (len bed) + lsum inflow0 label (nb - 1) (len bed)
  requires bsum bed label (nb - 1) (len bed) + bsum load label (nb - 1) (len bed) + bsum inflow label (nb - 1) (len bed) + gone.[nb - 1] =
    bsum bed0 label (nb - 1) (len bed) + bsum load0 label (nb - 1) (len bed) + bsum inflow0 label (nb - 1) (len bed)
  ensures lsum bed label nb (len bed) + lsum load label nb (len bed) + lsum inflow label nb (len bed) + sum gone nb =
    lsum bed0 label nb (len bed) + lsum load0 label nb (len bed) + lsum inflow0 label nb (len bed)
= lsum_split bed label nb (len bed); lsum_split load label nb (len bed); lsum_split inflow label nb (len bed);
  lsum_split bed0 label nb (len bed); lsum_split load0 label nb (len bed); lsum_split inflow0 label nb (len bed);
  assert sum gone nb = sum gone (nb - 1) + gone.[nb - 1];
  add_basin (lsum bed label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (lsum load label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (lsum inflow label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (sum gone (nb - 1))
    (lsum bed0 label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (lsum load0 label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (lsum inflow0 label (nb - 1) (len bed))
    (bsum bed label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (bsum load label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (bsum inflow label (nb - 1) (len bed)) gone.[nb - 1]
    (bsum bed0 label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (bsum load0 label (nb - 1) (len bed)) (bsum inflow0 label (nb - 1) (len bed))
    (lsum bed label nb (len bed)) (lsum load label nb (len bed)) (lsum inflow label nb (len bed)) (sum gone nb)
    (lsum bed0 label nb (len bed)) (lsum load0 label nb (len bed)) (lsum inflow0 label nb (len bed))

The per-basin laws, summed over the basins below nb.

let lemma lsum_balance (bed : [u32]) (load : [u32]) (inflow : [u32]) (bed0 : [u32]) (load0 : [u32]) (inflow0 : [u32])
    (gone : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (nb : usize) : unit
  requires len load = len bed && len inflow = len bed && len bed0 = len bed && len load0 = len bed
  requires len inflow0 = len bed && len label = len bed && len bed <= max u32 + 1
  requires nb <= len gone && len gone <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (b in 0 .. nb).
    bsum bed label b (len bed) + bsum load label b (len bed) + bsum inflow label b (len bed) + gone.[b] =
    bsum bed0 label b (len bed) + bsum load0 label b (len bed) + bsum inflow0 label b (len bed)
  ensures lsum bed label nb (len bed) + lsum load label nb (len bed) + lsum inflow label nb (len bed) + sum gone nb =
    lsum bed0 label nb (len bed) + lsum load0 label nb (len bed) + lsum inflow0 label nb (len bed)
  decreases nb
= if nb > 0 then (
    lsum_balance bed load inflow bed0 load0 inflow0 gone label (nb - 1);
    assert bsum bed label (nb - 1) (len bed) + bsum load label (nb - 1) (len bed) + bsum inflow label (nb - 1) (len bed) + gone.[nb - 1] =
      bsum bed0 label (nb - 1) (len bed) + bsum load0 label (nb - 1) (len bed) + bsum inflow0 label (nb - 1) (len bed);
    balance_step bed load inflow bed0 load0 inflow0 gone label nb)

A basin's sum is at most the whole sum.

let lemma bsum_le (xs : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (b : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires n <= len xs && len label = len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  ensures bsum xs label b n <= sum xs n
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then bsum_le xs label b (n - 1)

A basin's outflow is at most the whole map's total.

let lemma outflow_fits (a : u64) (b : u64) (c : u64) (g : u64) (a0 : u64) (b0 : u64) (c0 : u64) (s1 : u64) (s2 : u64) (s3 : u64) : unit
  requires a + b + c + g = a0 + b0 + c0
  requires a0 <= s1 && b0 <= s2 && c0 <= s3 && s1 + s2 + s3 <= max u32
  ensures g <= max u32
= ()

steps time steps over every basin at once, each basin on its own: a spread over the basins (ADR 0060), with the basin labels as the owner of bed, load, inflow and flux, and each basin's outflow in its own cell of gone_by. Each basin conserves its total, and the totals add up to the whole map's.

let transport_basins (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (border : [usize]) (label : [usize])
    (first : [usize]) (last : [usize]) (gowner : [usize]) (steps : u32)
    (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32])
    (flux : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (gone_by : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len border = len fill && len label = len fill
  requires len first = len fill && len last = len fill && len gowner = len fill && len gone_by = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len load = len fill && len inflow = len fill && len flux = len fill
  requires len fill <= max u32
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down).
             down.[k] = k || (down.[k] < len fill && fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len label). label.[at down k] = label.[k] && at label k < len fill
  requires forall (b in 0 .. len fill). first.[b] <= last.[b] && last.[b] <= len fill
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len border). border.[q] < len fill && label.[border.[q]] = at gowner q
  requires forall (b in 0 .. len fill) (q in 0 .. len border). first.[b] <= q && q < last.[b] ==> at gowner q = b
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len load). load.[k] = 0
  requires sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) <= max u32
  ensures sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + sum gone_by (len gone_by) =
    sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow)
= let n = len fill in
  spread b in 0 .. n @owns(bed, label) @owns(load, label) @owns(inflow, label) @owns(flux, label)
    ensures bsum bed label b n + bsum load label b n + bsum inflow label b n + gone_by.[b] =
      bsum (old bed) label b n + bsum (old load) label b n + bsum (old inflow) label b n
  do
    let lo = first.[b] in
    let hi = last.[b] in
    assert (forall (q in lo .. hi). border.[q] < n && label.[border.[q]] = b);
    bsum_le (old bed) label b n; bsum_le (old load) label b n; bsum_le (old inflow) label b n;
    let g : mutable u64 = 0 in
    for s in 0 .. steps
      invariant forall (k in 0 .. len load). label.[k] = b ==> load.[k] = 0
      invariant bsum bed label b n + bsum load label b n + bsum inflow label b n + g =
        bsum (old bed) label b n + bsum (old load) label b n + bsum (old inflow) label b n
    do
      g <- btransport fill down acc border label b lo hi bed load inflow flux g
    done;
    outflow_fits (bsum bed label b n) (bsum load label b n) (bsum inflow label b n) g
      (bsum (old bed) label b n) (bsum (old load) label b n) (bsum (old inflow) label b n)
      (sum (old bed) n) (sum (old load) n) (sum (old inflow) n);
    let gb : u32 = g in
    gone_by.[b] <- gb
  done;
  lsum_balance bed load inflow (old bed) (old load) (old inflow) gone_by label n;
  lsum_all bed label n n; lsum_all load label n n; lsum_all inflow label n n;
  lsum_all (old bed) label n n; lsum_all (old load) label n n; lsum_all (old inflow) label n n

steps time steps of sediment transport, every basin on its own core, from the sediment in bed with no load and no inflow. label, order and down come from the first half and from drainage (sediment.pia.md): every cell's basin is an outlet below len fill, a cell and the cell it drains to share a basin, and order names cells. The result is the mass that left the map, and the total is conserved exactly; if the total does not fit in a u32, nothing moves and the result is 2^64 - 1.

let sediment_basins (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (label : [usize]) (order : [usize]) (steps : u32)
    (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : out mutable [u32]) (inflow : out mutable [u32])
    (flux : out mutable [u32]) (gone_by : out mutable [u32])
    (border : out mutable [usize]) (keys : out mutable [usize]) (place2 : out mutable [usize]) (pos2 : out mutable [usize])
    (cnt : out mutable [u32]) (first : out mutable [usize]) (next : out mutable [usize]) (last : out mutable [usize])
    (gowner : out mutable [usize]) : u64
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len label = len fill && len order = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len load = len fill && len inflow = len fill && len flux = len fill && len gone_by = len fill
  requires len border = len fill && len keys = len fill && len place2 = len fill && len pos2 = len fill
  requires len cnt = len fill && len first = len fill && len next = len fill && len last = len fill && len gowner = len fill
  requires len fill >= 1 && len fill < max u32
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down).
             down.[k] = k || (down.[k] < len fill && fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len label). label.[at down k] = label.[k] && at label k < len fill
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len fill
  ensures result = max u64 ||
    sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + result = sum (old bed) (len bed)
=
  for i in 0 .. len fill
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. i). load.[k] = 0 && inflow.[k] = 0 && flux.[k] = 0 && gone_by.[k] = 0
  do
    load.[i] <- 0;
    inflow.[i] <- 0;
    flux.[i] <- 0;
    gone_by.[i] <- 0
  done;
  zero load (len load);
  zero inflow (len inflow);
  let t = total bed in
  if t > max u32 then max u64
  else (
    basin_order label order border keys place2 pos2 cnt first next last gowner;
    transport_basins fill down acc border label first last gowner steps bed load inflow flux gone_by;
    total gone_by)

docs.title: What is proved
docs.text: Goal Where Every index is in bounds, nothing overflows every function Grouping by basin puts exactly basin b's cells in its range of places ghistogram up to basin_order A write to a basin's cell changes its sum by the new value less the old, and a write elsewhere leaves it alone bupdate, bset, and bsum's frame lemma Each step in a basin conserves the basin's total bpush up to btransport No two basins touch the same cell, so the spread has no race the footprints and @owns(_, label) The basins' totals add up to the map's, and the map's total is conserved exactly lsum_balance, transport_basins, sediment_basins

docs.title: Codegen v0
docs.text:
Status: implemented in M6 (#7).

piac --emit=obj -o file.o file.pia verifies a program (verifier.md) and compiles it to an object file for Apple silicon (Mach-O) or Linux x86_64 (ELF) (ADR 0049). The result links with C. The other outputs stop earlier in the pipeline:

Flag Output --emit=core MLIR in arith, scf, memref and func, after contracts are erased --emit=llvm optimised LLVM IR --emit=asm assembly --emit=obj an object file, written to -o

--target=<triple> and --cpu=<name> choose the machine: arm64-apple-macosx14.0.0 with apple-m1, or x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with x86-64-v3. The default is the host piac was built for. x86-64-v3 is also the oldest x86_64 CPU piac accepts: a --cpu without AVX2, BMI1, BMI2, F16C, FMA, LZCNT and MOVBE is an error (ADR 0049). Bazel always passes both, for the platform it builds for (tools/piac/targets.bzl). -O0 to -O3 set the optimisation level, which defaults to -O2.

docs.title: Verification comes first
docs.text:
Code is generated only when every obligation is proved. If one fails, piac prints the report from --verify and stops. An obligation that is not proved either way, such as the termination of a while loop with no decreases measure, also stops it: piac lists each unproved obligation with its function and generates nothing.

To compile anyway, accept specific unproved obligations with --allow-unproved, which can be repeated:

Flag Accepts --allow-unproved=drain every unproved obligation in the function drain --allow-unproved=file.pia:30 the unproved obligations on line 30 --allow-unproved=file.pia:30:37 the one at line 30, column 37

The location is written the way piac prints it. Accepted obligations are still reported as a warning, and a flag that accepts nothing is reported too, so stale ones show up. A failed obligation cannot be accepted. piac --verify takes the same flag, and fails on a skipped goal that it does not accept.

docs.title: Stages
docs.text:
1. Erase contracts. Every pia_contract op is removed: requires, ensures, invariant, decreases, assert, assume and obligation. Then everything only they used is removed too, including quantifiers, old and the arithmetic inside contracts. An op that writes, or a loop or branch that calls a function which may write (one that takes a buffer, or any call but a spec function's inside it), stays even when only a contract reads its results (tests/codegen/contract_only_loop.pia). That includes calls to ordinary functions and loads: an op whose every use is in a contract, or in another such op, never runs, so it goes even when it is not known to be pure (a call to another module's function is a declaration here). Kept, such code could run a contract's xs.[result] when result = len xs, since a contract evaluates both sides of &&, and LLVM would treat the out-of-bounds load as undefined behaviour (tests/codegen/contract_only.pia). Only ops that write, allocate or free are kept. Spec functions and lemmas (pia.spec, pia.lemma) are erased with every call to them: they exist only for the verifier. The verifier's pia.proved attributes stay.
  2. Lower pia to core dialects. This uses MLIR dialect conversion, with the type mapping below and the ops after it. scf, func.call and func.return are converted structurally. Then each function marked @lower gets its MLIR form in place of its body (below).
  3. Lower to the llvm dialect. When a lowering was applied, convert-linalg-to-loops, expand-strided-metadata and lower-affine run first. Then the upstream passes run in this order: scf to cf, then cf, arith, index, memref and func to llvm, then the reconciliation of casts. Then each public function gets its C entry point.
  4. Translate and optimise. The module is translated to LLVM IR, given the target's data layout, and run through LLVM's -O2 pipeline.
  5. Emit. The LLVM target machine writes the object file or the assembly.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
A range type is stored in the smallest machine integer that holds its range: 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits. It is signed if the range contains a negative value. So u8 and int{0..200} become i8, i8 stays i8, and int{-1..200} becomes i16. bool is i1, and an index is index.

Pia Core MLIR !pia.int<lo, hi> iN, as above f32, f64 f32, f64 [T; n] memref<n x T> [T] memref<? x T, strided<[1], offset: ?>> !pia.atomic<T> memref<1 x T>, with a bool held as i8 !pia.rec<"tree"> !llvm.struct<"pia.rec.tree", (tag, fields...)> a mutable function reference, (u8) -> u8 (i8) -> i8, a pointer to the function

A mutable function reference (ADR 0071) is the address of the wrapper that checked its function against the arrow, func.constant @"succ@f.pia:5:74", and rebinding it replaces the value, so in a loop or a branch it is a phi of addresses. A call through it goes to the reference's proxy, h@f.pia:5:20, whose body is the func.call_indirect; the verifier takes the proxy's contract, the arrow's, as given, and LLVM inlines the proxy, leaving one indirect call.

A slice's offset is dynamic because xs.[a .. b] (pia.slice) is a view into the same storage: it lowers to memref.extract_strided_metadata and memref.reinterpret_cast, at the buffer's offset plus a, with b - a elements. At the C boundary a slice is still a pointer and a length, with offset 0. abort () lowers to llvm.intr.trap. A constant array (pia.const_array) becomes a private constant memref.global, one per constant, which LLVM places in read-only data; each use is a memref.get_global. A with_arena's region (pia.region) is a memref.alloca at the start of the function, zeroed by a loop where the with_arena is entered.

An array result is a buffer the caller makes. Arrays are values, and a function's own arrays live in its frame, so arrayResultsToBuffers (src/codegen/ArrayResults.cpp) runs first: each function whose results include arrays, a record result's array fields among them once records are scalarized, takes one more parameter per array result, each return copies the array into it (pia.copy, a memref.copy), and each call makes the buffer in its caller's frame (pia.region, an alloca at the function's entry) and reads the result from it. The verifier runs before this, on the value form. A foreign function cannot return an array yet, and an exported function that returns one takes the buffer as a pointer after its other parameters. Records are scalarized before codegen (irgen.md). A buffer of records arrives as one buffer per field (struct of arrays), so [pixel; 8] is four memref<8 x i8>, which vectorises like any other buffer. A buffer whose elements are slices, such as a vector's box slots, becomes two buffers before lowering, splitSliceBuffers in src/codegen/SliceBuffers.cpp (ADR 0048, step 3): its elements' addresses and their lengths, both memref<? x index>, the lengths marked {pia.length_of} the addresses. Storing a slice records pia.address, its storage's aligned pointer plus its offset in bytes, and its length; loading one rebuilds it from both with pia.at_address, a memref descriptor at that address with offset 0. The store that empties an element moved out (pia.moved_out) is code like any other, so a moved-out element's length is 0 at run time, as the proof has it. Buffers of buffers of slices and dyn are not lowered yet.

A recursive value (ADR 0047, step 3) is laid out as a variant is: an identified LLVM struct, pia.rec.tree, of its tag, then each constructor's payload fields in order, the payload's record leaves as scalarization gives them. A buffer in a payload, such as a box's slot or a vec's items, is its memref descriptor, so a recursive occurrence is a pointer and a length into memory an allocator lent, and the struct is never part of itself. pia.rec_make is llvm.mlir.zero with the tag and the payload inserted, pia.rec_tag and pia.rec_payload extract them, and a buffer of recursive values is a memref of the struct, which loads and stores as any element (MLIR is told it may be one). Building a node allocates its boxes explicitly, through its allocator, so every allocation is visible and fallible, and a tree lives in whatever region its allocator draws from: tests/codegen/rec_run.pia builds one in cells its C caller lends and sums it (rec_run_test.c), and tests/std/rec_mem.pia does the same with Pia.Mem's box and bump. A function that takes or returns a recursive value by value has no C entry point, since the struct has no C type yet; C passes a buffer of them. Dropping a recursive value frees nothing: every allocator so far is a region's (bump, arena), whose memory goes when the region does, so no drop runs, and none can use stack. The iterative drop of ADR 0047, section 4, comes with the first allocator that frees one block at a time (ADR 0046, step 2).

docs.title: Arithmetic
docs.text:
Each pia.add, sub, mul, div and rem is computed at one width. That width holds both operands and the result type. Unless the result was proved to fit, it also holds the exact result. The operands are extended by their own signedness, and the operation is signed if anything at that width can be negative. Then the overflow mode brings the exact value into the result type:

Mode Lowering proof nothing: the verifier proved the value fits, so the result is truncated saturate clamp to [lo, hi] with max and min, then truncate wrap truncate when the type covers a whole machine integer, as u8 and i32 do. Otherwise lo + ((x - lo) mod size) trap llvm.intr.trap if the value is outside [lo, hi]

pia.convert is the same with the input as the exact value. pia.cmp extends both sides to a width that holds both ranges. to_index and from_index become index_cast (or index_castui when the value is non-negative). len becomes memref.dim, or a constant for a fixed array. load and store become memref.load and memref.store, without bounds checks, because the verifier proved them in bounds.

Floats are already core MLIR: IRGen emits arith.addf, subf, mulf, divf, negf, cmpf and float arith.constant directly, with no fast-math flags, so each operation is one IEEE 754 operation rounded to nearest (ADR 0004, ADR 0012). Nothing reassociates them, and LLVM contracts a * b + c into an FMA only when both operations carry the contract flag, which IRGen never sets, and Pia never sets flush-to-zero, so subnormals are kept. = is cmpf oeq and <> is cmpf une, so with a NaN every comparison is false but <>. Conversions are pia ops that lower to LLVM's: f32 n of an integer is sitofp or uitofp by the signedness of its storage, f64 x and f32 x between the widths are arith.extf and arith.truncf, i32 x of a float is fptosi or fptoui at the target's storage width, whose result the verifier proved is in range so it is never poison, and to_bits and from_bits are arith.bitcast. tests/codegen/floats.pia checks this against C compiled with -ffp-contract=off, bit for bit (floats_test.c).

LLVM recognises the widen-clamp-truncate pattern, so add_px on u8 with @overflow(saturate) compiles to llvm.uadd.sat.i8. In a loop over slices, such as add_rows in tests/codegen/saturate.pia, LLVM's loop vectoriser turns it into NEON uqadd.16b.

docs.title: Atomics
docs.text:
An atomic cell is a one-element memref (ADR 0052, section 5). atomic_new is a memref.alloca at the start of the function and a plain store, since nothing else sees the cell yet. Every other op is an LLVM atomic on the memref's aligned pointer, at the element's alignment: llvm.load and llvm.store with an ordering, llvm.atomicrmw, llvm.cmpxchg (whose old value is the result) and llvm.fence. relaxed is LLVM's monotonic, and the other orders keep their names. atomic_min and atomic_max are min and max on a signed cell, umin and umax otherwise. A bool is a byte, since LLVM's atomics take whole bytes.

An add or sub lowers by its stated mode. wrap and proof are one atomicrmw. trap is one too, after which the exact result is computed from the old value it returns, at twice the cell's width, and checked as trap arithmetic is, so the cell already holds the wrapped value when the program stops. saturate is a loop: a relaxed load, then cmpxchg of the old value for the clamped result until no other task changed the cell in between, so no wrapped value is ever stored. The loop's failure order is the read half of the op's order.

LLVM's backends choose the instructions, which are those of ADR 0052's table. tests/codegen/atomics.pia compiles one function per (operation, order) for both targets and checks the instructions with FileCheck. Both targets detect a trap overflow from the old value for now; the target model's rmw_flags records that x86_64's lock xadd sets the flags, for a lowering that reads them. The x86_64 lowering of relaxed inside @target(x86_64_linux) items, and its check, are a later step (ADR 0052, section 6).

docs.title: C ABI
docs.text:
Each Pia function f becomes an internal function. Only the functions a module exports through an interface also get a C entry point (ADR 0039): one in an interface marked @abi(c) is named f, and one in any other interface is named after its module's path, so luma in module Image.Pixels is pia$Image$Pixels$luma. A file with no module header exports nothing but its main. Private functions keep internal linkage, so LLVM can inline them and remove the ones nothing calls. An exported function also keeps its Pia calling convention under its module's link symbol, __pia$Image$Pixels$luma, which is what another module calls when it imports the function: the importer's object file declares that symbol and has no body for it, so the two object files must be linked together (the pia_library rule does this). Calls between Pia functions use the internal one, which takes MLIR memref descriptors. The entry point maps C arguments onto it:

Pia parameter C parameters an integer the integer type of its storage width, such as uint8_t or int16_t bool bool f32, f64 float, double [T] const T *data, uint64_t len (or T * when it is written) [T; n] const T *data (or T *)

A record parameter is passed as its fields, in declaration order, so blend (p : pixel) (q : pixel) : pixel takes eight uint8_t arguments. A record result is written through a pointer to a C struct of its fields, which is the last argument; a record that flattens to one scalar, such as a one-field record or a distinct type (ADR 0064), returns that scalar instead. Each field sits at its natural C offset, aligned to its own size:

struct pixel { uint8_t r, g, b, a; };
void blend(uint8_t pr, uint8_t pg, uint8_t pb, uint8_t pa,
           uint8_t qr, uint8_t qg, uint8_t qb, uint8_t qa, struct pixel *out);

A buffer of records is passed as one buffer per field, in declaration order. A slice of records has one length, passed after its first field's pointer, which every field buffer shares ({pia.length_of} marks the others):

// opaque_all (xs : out mutable [pixel]) (v : u8) : unit
void opaque_all(uint8_t *r, uint64_t n, uint8_t *g, uint8_t *b, uint8_t *a,
                uint8_t v);

A buffer of slices is passed the same way, as the buffer of its elements' addresses and the buffer of their lengths, which shares the first's count (tests/codegen/slice_buffers_run.pia, run by slice_buffers_run_test.c):

// first (xs : borrowed [[u16]]) : u16
uint16_t first(uint64_t *addr, int64_t n, uint64_t *len);

Integers narrower than 32 bits are marked zeroext or signext, as the Apple arm64 ABI requires and as clang and GCC do for x86_64 System V. Signedness comes from the range type. Once a range type is lowered to a signless iN, its signedness would be lost, so lowerToCore records it as a {pia.signed} argument or result attribute. Unit results are void. A prime cannot appear in a C name, so each ' in a function's name becomes _prime in its entry point: step' is called as step_prime. Two functions whose C names would be the same are an error. Returning a buffer is not supported yet.

For example, add_rows (a : [u8]) (b : [u8]) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : unit is called from C as:

void add_rows(const uint8_t *a, uint64_t na, const uint8_t *b, uint64_t nb,
              uint8_t *dst, uint64_t ndst);

docs.title: Spec-only state
docs.text: A parameter, local or record field whose type is spec-only (int, real or a theory's sort) is state the verifier sees and the program does not have (ADR 0041). Code can only store spec values in such places, so nothing the program computes reads them. eraseContracts replaces every computation of a spec-only value left in code, such as Alloc.take t.heap b stored into a field, with pia.erased, and marks the spec-only parameters and results {pia.erased}. lowerToCore lowers each spec-only value to an i1 that nothing reads, and LLVM removes it. The C entry points leave spec-only parameters and fields out: skip (n : int) (x : u8) : u8 is uint8_t skip(uint8_t x), and a result { v : u8; steps : int } is returned as its one remaining field, a uint8_t. A spec-only field of a buffer's records is a buffer of its own, struct of arrays like every field: eraseContracts removes the stores into it, its loads are spec-only values like any other, and it is marked {pia.erased}. Its C entry point leaves it out, and when the fields share one length the first field kept takes it, so [{ steps : int; v : u8 }] is uint8_t *v, int64_t n, and len xs reads the length of a field in code. Spec state (ADR 0058), a let spec local or a spec parameter, is spec-only whatever its type, so it cannot be erased by type: IRGen marks a spec local's pia.region and a spec parameter's argument {pia.spec_state}. Code only writes spec state, and only contracts read it, so once the contracts are gone eraseSpecState erases every op that uses spec state, and every op that uses one of those. A call passes spec state only for a spec parameter, so the pass removes each spec parameter, from definitions and declarations alike, and the argument each call passes for it. A spec field's leaves, once ScalarizeRecords splits a record, are spec parameters and spec results ({pia.spec_state}): the pass removes those results from functions, returns and calls, re-points a slice of records' pia.length_of when the field it named goes, and follows spec state through scf.for, scf.while and scf.if, where the value a loop or branch still carries becomes pia.erased (a one-byte view in place of an erased buffer). tests/codegen/spec_state.pia is run from C by spec_state_test.c.

docs.title: Foreign functions
docs.text:
let f (x : i32) : i32 ensures ... = extern "sym" declares a C function (#55). IRGen makes f a private function whose whole body is pia.foreign "sym"(...), marked pia.extern, so callers see its contract like any other function's: preconditions are proved at each call and postconditions are assumed. The verifier never proves the stub itself; the contract is trusted, and piac --verify --trust-report lists it.

A foreign function without a requires or ensures can be called only as unsafe f x. The call is marked pia.unsafe: the verifier assumes nothing about its result beyond its type, and treats every buffer passed to it as written. --trust-report lists each such call site.

Codegen declares sym once, as a private function with C types, and calls it. An integer keeps its width, extended to 32 bits as Apple's arm64 ABI and x86_64 System V expect (llvm.zeroext or llvm.signext), and a bool is a zero-extended i1. A buffer is passed as a pointer to its first element, which for a view (xs.[a .. b]) is part way into its storage; pass its length as a separate usize argument. If the Pia declaration has the same name as the symbol, it is renamed pia$ffi$sym. For now a foreign function takes integers, bools and buffers of integers, and returns an integer, a bool or unit. tests/codegen/ffi_run.pia runs against C in ffi_test.c.

A C variadic function, such as open or syscall, is declared with @variadic(n) after the return type, where n is the number of its named C parameters (ADR 0051). Codegen declares the symbol as an llvm.func with ... and emits each call as llvm.call ... vararg(...), so LLVM applies the variadic convention: Apple arm64 passes the arguments after the named ones on the stack, and x86_64 System V sets %al. Several declarations may call one symbol at different arities, such as open and open_mode, as long as they agree on n and on the named parameters. A variadic argument must be an integer of 32 bits or more, or a buffer, because C promotes anything narrower to an int, and IRGen says to widen it rather than doing it silently. tests/codegen/ffi_variadic.pia checks the lowering, and ffi_run.pia runs two arities of one symbol and a buffer passed through ... against C.

A C function that returns a pointer to an integer, such as glibc's __errno_location or Darwin's __error, is declared with @deref after the return type, which is the integer's type (ADR 0057, section 5). Codegen declares the symbol as an llvm.func returning ptr and follows each call with an llvm.load of the result, so the pointer never reaches Pia. Pia.Sys.Posix.errno is the one such row. ffi_run.pia reads a counter through one after a call that changes it.

A C function of no arguments, such as getpid, is declared like any Pia function of none, let getpid () : i32 = extern "getpid", and called by its name alone, getpid.

The POSIX declarations are not written by hand. tools/bindings/gen.py reads the names in tools/bindings/posix.toml from the target's own headers with clang's JSON AST, and the rows of the Posix interface in lib/Pia/Sys/Posix.pia, and writes lib/Pia/Sys/Gen/<target>.pia, the module Pia.Sys.Posix for that target (ADR 0057). It holds every constant's value and C type, every struct's size, alignment and field offsets, each row of the interface as an extern with the row's modifiers and contract, and the other functions as externs without one, which stay private to the module. A row that does not fit the header fails the generator: a missing symbol, a type of the wrong width, mutable or out on a const pointer, or a variadic mismatch. A pointer becomes a byte buffer. A function Pia cannot declare yet, such as mmap, which returns a pointer, is listed at the end of the file with the reason. The bindings workflow regenerates each file on its own platform and fails on any difference, and the build picks the file by platform (//lib/Pia/Sys:posix).

Foreign memory comes back as an address, a usize, and unsafe view addr n makes it a slice (pia.view, marked pia.unsafe). Codegen builds the memref descriptor an LLVM lowering of a memref expects, with addr as its pointer, offset 0, n elements and stride 1, so loads, stores and slices of it lower as usual. tests/codegen/pages.pia fills and sums pages from mmap.

docs.title: Lowerings written in Pia
docs.text:
@lower("mlir") after a function's return type gives it an MLIR form (ADR 0065). The Pia body stays: the verifier proves it against the contract as usual, callers prove from the contract, and the body is what the REPL's JIT runs and what piac --lower=off compiles everywhere, for differential tests. Codegen puts the MLIR in place of the body:

let matmul (a : [i8; 16]) (b : [i8; 16]) (c : out mutable [i32; 16]) : unit
  @lower("%a = memref.expand_shape $a [[0, 1]] output_shape [4, 4] : $a.type into memref<4x4xi8>  %b = memref.expand_shape $b [[0, 1]] output_shape [4, 4] : $b.type into memref<4x4xi8>  %c = memref.expand_shape $c [[0, 1]] output_shape [4, 4] : $c.type into memref<4x4xi32>  %zero = arith.constant 0 : i32  linalg.fill ins(%zero : i32) outs(%c : memref<4x4xi32>)  linalg.matmul ins(%a, %b : memref<4x4xi8>, memref<4x4xi8>) outs(%c : memref<4x4xi32>)")
= for i in 0 .. 4 do
    for j in 0 .. 4 do
      c.[i * 4 + j] <- a.[i * 4] * b.[j] + a.[i * 4 + 1] * b.[4 + j]
        + a.[i * 4 + 2] * b.[8 + j] + a.[i * 4 + 3] * b.[12 + j]
    done
  done
  • Splices. $name is the SSA value of the parameter name, and $name.type its core MLIR type from the table above, so $a.type here is memref<16xi8>. A spliced parameter is an integer, a bool, or a buffer of them, which is one value. A record is several values, and is refused unless its type has @lower. Escapes in the string are decoded first (\n, \t, \", \\), and MLIR needs no newlines between ops.
  • Types. @lower("memref<4x4xi8>", data) on a record names the MLIR type its values have, as a view of the field that holds its elements (ADR 0074, step 3a). In the type, $n splices a value parameter, $s a shape as 4x4, and $t the elements' type parameter, so grid i32 [4; 4] r below has memref<4x4xi32>. A lowering that splices a value of the type gets the view, made before the lowering's own ops. An array field is viewed with memref.expand_shape, so $a.type is memref<4x4xi8>. A slice field may start part way into its storage, so it is cast to its length and viewed with a dynamic offset, memref<4x4xi32, strided<[4, 1], offset: ?>>. The body proves that length from the type's invariant: a goal at each such parameter says that 'c.data' holds 16 elements. An out or inout value of such a type is written through its loan and comes back as it went in, so codegen returns it, and the function returns unit. An out or inout value of any other type would come back changed, which MLIR text cannot say, so it is refused. Version 1 is a ranked memref with static extents and the identity layout. tensor comes with step 3b. The views are part of the hashed text in the trust report.
let mat8 = type { data : [i8; 16] } @lower("memref<4x4xi8>", data)

let grid = let (t : type) (s : shape) (r : region) => type {
  data : borrowed(r) mutable [t]
} where len s = 2 && len data = s.[0] * s.[1]
  @lower("memref<$s x $t>", data)

let matmul (r : region) (a : mat8) (b : mat8) (c : inout grid i32 [4; 4] r)
  : unit
  @lower("%zero = arith.constant 0 : i32\nlinalg.fill ins(%zero : i32) outs($c : $c.type)\nlinalg.matmul ins($a, $b : $a.type, $b.type) outs($c : $c.type)")
= ...
  • Computed lowerings. @lower(gen args), where gen is a let meta that returns a string, runs gen during expansion (meta.md), and the string becomes the attribute's text, as if it were written there; piac --dump-expanded shows it. In the arguments, the function's parameters stand for themselves, as names, as a tactic's do, so name a is "a". So one metaprogram can write the MLIR for several shapes or element types: tests/codegen/lower_meta.pia computes the matmul above with @lower(square_matmul 4 a b c "i8" "i32"). A metaprogram that fails, or returns anything but a string, is an error at the attribute.
  • Parsing. After lowerToCore, applyLowerings (src/codegen/Lowerings.cpp) splices in the core arguments, wraps the text as the body of func.func @pia_lowering with the function's core signature, adds return when the function returns nothing (one that returns an integer or a bool ends with its own return), and parses and verifies it with MLIR's parser against the dialects piac registers: linalg, tensor, bufferization, transform, affine and the core ones. A misspelt op or a type that does not match is an error at the attribute, with MLIR's message and its line and column in the spliced text, which a note prints. The parsed body then replaces the function's, with every op located at the attribute, so a later error points there too. --emit=core shows the lowered form, linalg included.
  • Checked first. The same splice and parse, and the operand-effect check below, run on a copy of the module as soon as IRGen has made it, before anything is proved, in every mode that makes IR (--emit=mlir, --verify, codegen) and in the REPL, whose JIT still runs the body (checkLowerings). So a mistake in the MLIR costs no proving time. A module that lowerToCore cannot compile yet is not checked there; codegen says why if it is compiled.
  • Operand effects. A lowering may write only the buffers the Pia signature lets it write: those of out and inout parameters, and the buffers codegen adds, such as an array result's. Every op's memory effects are read through MLIR's MemoryEffectOpInterface, following memref's views (expand_shape, subview, reinterpret_cast, cast) back to the parameter, so a linalg op whose outs view an input, a memref.store into one, or a memref.dealloc of one is an error that names the op and the parameter. An op with no declared effects that takes an input buffer is refused too, since it could write it. Reading inputs and writing the lowering's own allocas is allowed (tests/irgen/lower_effects.pia).
  • Passes. linalg on memrefs goes to scf loops with convert-linalg-to-loops, then memref.expand_shape and the other reshapes to plain descriptors with expand-strided-metadata, and affine to arith with lower-affine, before the usual passes. tensor ops parse, but nothing bufferises them yet (step 6 of the ADR), so a lowering works on the buffers' memrefs.
  • Trust. In steps 1 and 2 of ADR 0065 piac does not yet prove that the MLIR does what the body does, so @lower is allowed only in a file marked @trusted, on a function with a Pia body (not an extern, a spec function or a lemma), and every lowering is a trusted item. piac --verify --trust-report lists it with the ops it uses and the SHA-256 of its spliced text, and the object's certificate records the same hash (abi.md). A named linalg op's own body is generated from its definition, so the ops in it are not listed; a linalg.generic's are.

linalg.matmul adds to its output, so the lowering fills it with zero first, as the body's assignments do; without the fill the differential run below fails, which is the check a trusted lowering has. tests/codegen/lower_linalg.pia is the matmul above, checked at --emit=core with and without --lower=off, in the trust report and in the certificate, and run from C in lower_linalg_test.c, once from each form. tests/codegen/lower_meta.pia computes the same lowering with a metaprogram and is run from the same harness (lower_meta_run_test). tests/codegen/lower_type.pia lowers the matmul over a lowered array type and a lowered slice type. tests/codegen/lower_invalid.pia holds MLIR errors, tests/irgen/lower_effects.pia the operand-effect check, and tests/irgen/lower_errors.pia, lower_meta_errors.pia, lower_untrusted.pia, lower_type_errors.pia and lower_type_inout_errors.pia the rules.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• tests/codegen/*.pia are lit tests. They check --emit=core and --emit=llvm, the refusal to compile a program with a failed or unproved obligation, and --allow-unproved. They run on any host: the lit runner compiles for arm64-apple-macosx14.0.0 unless a RUN line passes its own --target, so the expected IR is the same everywhere.
  • //tests/codegen:saturate_test compiles saturate.pia to an object file and links it with saturate_test.c. The harness compares saturating, wrapping and proof-mode arithmetic, a slice loop and a fixed array against C reference implementations. The 8-bit cases cover every input. The test runs on arm64 macOS and on x86_64 Linux. On other platforms Bazel skips it as incompatible.

docs.title: Limits of v0
docs.text:
• There is no vectorisation yet. Loops compile to scalar code, apart from whatever LLVM's own vectoriser does with them.
  • dyn, buffers nested deeper than a buffer of slices, and buffer results are not lowered.
  • A recursive value's layout keeps every constructor's fields side by side, and a box's slot as a whole memref descriptor; the published union layout of ADR 0030, a box as one pointer and option (box t) as a nullable one, comes later.
  • An atomic cell crosses the C boundary as a pointer to its element, like a one-element array.
  • scf.for compares its bounds as signed 64-bit integers, so a slice of 2^63 elements or more is not supported.

docs.title: Pia and other verified languages
docs.text: Pia is not the first language to prove programs correct, and it borrows from most of the ones on this page. This page says, for each of the closest languages and tools, what they share with Pia, where Pia differs, and where they are ahead. It tries to be specific and fair: every one of them is more mature than Pia, which has not reached a 0.1 release (status).

docs.title: In one table
docs.text:
