let load_after (i : u64) (cap : u32) (bed : u32) : u32
  requires i + bed <= max u32
  ensures result = P.el i cap bed
= if i < cap then (let room = cap - i in if room < bed then cap else i + bed)
  else cap

docs.title: 3. A wave
docs.text:
The cells at positions lo .. hi of the height order, one thread each. Thread q writes only slot q of gathered, newbed and newout, the identity ownership of a spread, and every slot then holds what ready_init in pull.pia.md asks of a wave.

let wave (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (w : usize)
    (bed0 : [u32]) (flux : [u32]) (lo : usize) (hi : usize)
    (gathered : borrowed inout mutable [u64]) (newbed : borrowed inout mutable [u32])
    (newout : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len order = len fill
  requires len bed0 = len fill && len flux = len fill
  requires len gathered = len fill && len newbed = len fill && len newout = len fill
  requires lo <= hi && hi <= len fill && w >= 3 && w < max usize
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len fill
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len fill
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] = k || fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k]
  ensures forall (q in lo .. hi). gathered.[q] = P.inflow_of down flux w (order.[q])
  ensures forall (q in lo .. hi). gathered.[q] + bed0.[order.[q]] <= max u32 ==>
    newbed.[q] = P.eb (gathered.[q]) (P.cap_of fill down acc (order.[q])) (bed0.[order.[q]])
    && newout.[q] = P.el (gathered.[q]) (P.cap_of fill down acc (order.[q])) (bed0.[order.[q]])
= spread q in lo .. hi
    ensures gathered.[q] = P.inflow_of down flux w (order.[q])
    ensures gathered.[q] + bed0.[order.[q]] <= max u32 ==>
      newbed.[q] = P.eb (gathered.[q]) (P.cap_of fill down acc (order.[q])) (bed0.[order.[q]])
      && newout.[q] = P.el (gathered.[q]) (P.cap_of fill down acc (order.[q])) (bed0.[order.[q]])
  do
    let c = order.[q] in
    let g = gather down flux w c in
    gathered.[q] <- g;
    let b = bed0.[c] in
    let d = down.[c] in
    let drop : u16 = if d = c then 0 else fill.[c] - fill.[d] in
    if g + b <= max u32 then (
      let cap = capacity_of acc.[c] drop in
      newbed.[q] <- bed_after g cap b;
      newout.[q] <- load_after g cap b
    ) else (
      newbed.[q] <- b;
      newout.[q] <- 0
    )
  done

docs.title: 4. Its commit, on the GPU too
docs.text:
pull.pia.md commits a wave one cell at a time, in order. Here the commit is a spread as well: thread q writes cell order.[q] of bed, flux and seen, and pos is the owner array that says so, since pos.[order.[q]] = q (@owns, ADR 0060). After the spread, the cells of other waves keep their values, because no thread of this wave owns them.

The commit keeps the step's two invariants, for the whole wave at once. What makes that true is that a wave is one height. Every cell of the wave drains into a lower cell or into itself, so no cell processed so far, which is at that height or higher, reads a load the wave changed.

A load that changes only at cells of height v leaves the inflow of every cell at height v or higher as it was, one direction at a time:

let lemma wframe_dir (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (flux : [u32]) (flux2 : [u32]) (w : usize) (v : u16) (d : int{0..7}) : unit
  requires len fill = len down && len flux = len down && len flux2 = len down && w >= 3 && w < max usize
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len down && (down.[k] = k || fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (j in 0 .. len down). flux2.[j] = flux.[j] || fill.[j] = v
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len down). fill.[k] >= v ==> P.from down flux2 w k d = P.from down flux w k d
  with P.from
= ()

let lemma wframe_pair (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (flux : [u32]) (flux2 : [u32]) (w : usize) (v : u16) (h : int{0..3}) : unit
  requires len fill = len down && len flux = len down && len flux2 = len down && w >= 3 && w < max usize
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len down && (down.[k] = k || fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (j in 0 .. len down). flux2.[j] = flux.[j] || fill.[j] = v
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len down). fill.[k] >= v ==> P.pair down flux2 w k h = P.pair down flux w k h
= if h = 0 then (wframe_dir fill down flux flux2 w v 0; wframe_dir fill down flux flux2 w v 1)
  else if h = 1 then (wframe_dir fill down flux flux2 w v 2; wframe_dir fill down flux flux2 w v 3)
  else if h = 2 then (wframe_dir fill down flux flux2 w v 4; wframe_dir fill down flux flux2 w v 5)
  else (wframe_dir fill down flux flux2 w v 6; wframe_dir fill down flux flux2 w v 7)

let lemma wframe_all (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (flux : [u32]) (flux2 : [u32]) (w : usize) (v : u16) : unit
  requires len fill = len down && len flux = len down && len flux2 = len down && w >= 3 && w < max usize
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len down && (down.[k] = k || fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (j in 0 .. len down). flux2.[j] = flux.[j] || fill.[j] = v
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len down). fill.[k] >= v ==> P.inflow_of down flux2 w k = P.inflow_of down flux w k
  with P.inflow_of
= wframe_pair fill down flux flux2 w v 0; wframe_pair fill down flux flux2 w v 1;
  wframe_pair fill down flux flux2 w v 2; wframe_pair fill down flux flux2 w v 3

Every cell processed by the end of the wave is at height v or higher:

let lemma above (fill : [u16]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (lo : usize) (hi : usize) (v : u16) : unit
  requires len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len pos && pos.[order.[r]] = r
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
  requires forall (r in lo .. hi). fill.[P.at order r] = v
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len fill). P.at pos k < hi ==> fill.[k] >= v
=
  assert fill.[order.[lo]] = v;
  assert (forall (k in 0 .. len fill). P.at pos k < lo ==> fill.[order.[lo]] <= fill.[order.[P.at pos k]]);
  assert (forall (k in 0 .. len fill). P.at pos k < hi ==> order.[P.at pos k] = k)

The cells the commit changed are the wave's, which are at height v:

let lemma changed_in_wave (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (w : usize) (bed0 : [u32])
    (gathered : [u64]) (newbed : [u32]) (newout : [u32])
    (bed : [u32]) (flux : [u32]) (seen : [u64]) (bed2 : [u32]) (flux2 : [u32]) (seen2 : [u64])
    (lo : usize) (hi : usize) (v : u16) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len bed0 = len fill
  requires len gathered = len fill && len newbed = len fill && len newout = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len flux = len fill && len seen = len fill
  requires len bed2 = len fill && len flux2 = len fill && len seen2 = len fill
  requires w >= 3 && w < max usize && lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len pos && pos.[order.[r]] = r
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (r in lo .. hi). fill.[P.at order r] = v
  requires forall (q in lo .. hi). seen2.[P.at order q] = gathered.[q] && bed2.[P.at order q] = newbed.[q] && flux2.[P.at order q] = newout.[q]
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len fill). (P.at pos k < lo || P.at pos k >= hi) ==>
    bed2.[k] = bed.[k] && flux2.[k] = flux.[k] && seen2.[k] = seen.[k]
  ensures forall (j in 0 .. len fill). flux2.[j] = flux.[j] || fill.[j] = v
  ensures forall (j in 0 .. len fill). (lo <= P.at pos j && P.at pos j < hi) ==> P.at order (P.at pos j) = j
=
  assert (forall (j in 0 .. len fill). (lo <= P.at pos j && P.at pos j < hi) ==> P.at order (P.at pos j) = j);
  assert (forall (j in 0 .. len fill). (lo <= P.at pos j && P.at pos j < hi) ==> fill.[j] = v)

The committed cells keep the step's promise, holds_if:

let lemma done_commit (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (w : usize) (bed0 : [u32])
    (gathered : [u64]) (newbed : [u32]) (newout : [u32])
    (bed : [u32]) (flux : [u32]) (seen : [u64]) (bed2 : [u32]) (flux2 : [u32]) (seen2 : [u64])
    (lo : usize) (hi : usize) (v : u16) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len bed0 = len fill
  requires len gathered = len fill && len newbed = len fill && len newout = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len flux = len fill && len seen = len fill
  requires len bed2 = len fill && len flux2 = len fill && len seen2 = len fill
  requires w >= 3 && w < max usize && lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len pos && pos.[order.[r]] = r
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (q in lo .. hi). seen2.[P.at order q] = gathered.[q] && bed2.[P.at order q] = newbed.[q] && flux2.[P.at order q] = newout.[q]
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len fill). (P.at pos k < lo || P.at pos k >= hi) ==>
    bed2.[k] = bed.[k] && flux2.[k] = flux.[k] && seen2.[k] = seen.[k]
  requires P.done_if_upto fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen pos lo
  requires P.ready_vals fill down acc order bed0 gathered newbed newout lo hi
  ensures P.done_if_upto fill down acc bed0 bed2 flux2 seen2 pos hi
  with P.done_if_upto, P.ready_vals
=
  assert (forall (j in 0 .. len fill). (lo <= P.at pos j && P.at pos j < hi) ==> P.at order (P.at pos j) = j)

And they are linked: each took its upstream neighbours' loads.

let lemma linked_commit (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (w : usize) (bed0 : [u32])
    (gathered : [u64]) (newbed : [u32]) (newout : [u32])
    (bed : [u32]) (flux : [u32]) (seen : [u64]) (bed2 : [u32]) (flux2 : [u32]) (seen2 : [u64])
    (lo : usize) (hi : usize) (v : u16) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len bed0 = len fill
  requires len gathered = len fill && len newbed = len fill && len newout = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len flux = len fill && len seen = len fill
  requires len bed2 = len fill && len flux2 = len fill && len seen2 = len fill
  requires w >= 3 && w < max usize && lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len pos && pos.[order.[r]] = r
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len fill && (down.[k] = k || fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (r in lo .. hi). fill.[P.at order r] = v
  requires forall (q in lo .. hi). seen2.[P.at order q] = gathered.[q] && bed2.[P.at order q] = newbed.[q] && flux2.[P.at order q] = newout.[q]
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len fill). (P.at pos k < lo || P.at pos k >= hi) ==>
    bed2.[k] = bed.[k] && flux2.[k] = flux.[k] && seen2.[k] = seen.[k]
  requires P.linked_upto down flux seen pos lo w
  requires P.ready_in down order w flux gathered lo hi
  requires forall (j in 0 .. len fill). flux2.[j] = flux.[j] || fill.[j] = v
  requires forall (j in 0 .. len fill). (lo <= P.at pos j && P.at pos j < hi) ==> P.at order (P.at pos j) = j
  ensures P.linked_upto down flux2 seen2 pos hi w
  with P.linked_upto, P.ready_in
=
  wframe_all fill down flux flux2 w v;
  above fill order pos lo hi v

let lemma committed (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (w : usize) (bed0 : [u32])
    (gathered : [u64]) (newbed : [u32]) (newout : [u32])
    (bed : [u32]) (flux : [u32]) (seen : [u64]) (bed2 : [u32]) (flux2 : [u32]) (seen2 : [u64])
    (lo : usize) (hi : usize) (v : u16) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len bed0 = len fill
  requires len gathered = len fill && len newbed = len fill && len newout = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len flux = len fill && len seen = len fill
  requires len bed2 = len fill && len flux2 = len fill && len seen2 = len fill
  requires w >= 3 && w < max usize && lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len pos && pos.[order.[r]] = r
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len fill && (down.[k] = k || fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (r in lo .. hi). fill.[P.at order r] = v
  requires P.done_if_upto fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen pos lo
  requires P.linked_upto down flux seen pos lo w
  requires P.ready_in down order w flux gathered lo hi
  requires P.ready_vals fill down acc order bed0 gathered newbed newout lo hi
  requires forall (q in lo .. hi). seen2.[P.at order q] = gathered.[q] && bed2.[P.at order q] = newbed.[q] && flux2.[P.at order q] = newout.[q]
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len fill). (P.at pos k < lo || P.at pos k >= hi) ==>
    bed2.[k] = bed.[k] && flux2.[k] = flux.[k] && seen2.[k] = seen.[k]
  ensures P.done_if_upto fill down acc bed0 bed2 flux2 seen2 pos hi
  ensures P.linked_upto down flux2 seen2 pos hi w
=
  changed_in_wave fill down acc order pos w bed0 gathered newbed newout bed flux seen bed2 flux2 seen2 lo hi v;
  done_commit fill down acc order pos w bed0 gathered newbed newout bed flux seen bed2 flux2 seen2 lo hi v;
  linked_commit fill down acc order pos w bed0 gathered newbed newout bed flux seen bed2 flux2 seen2 lo hi v

The commit itself:

let commit (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (w : usize) (bed0 : [u32])
    (gathered : [u64]) (newbed : [u32]) (newout : [u32])
    (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (flux : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (seen : borrowed inout mutable [u64])
    (lo : usize) (hi : usize) (v : u16) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len bed0 = len fill
  requires len gathered = len fill && len newbed = len fill && len newout = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len flux = len fill && len seen = len fill
  requires w >= 3 && w < max usize && lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len pos && pos.[order.[r]] = r
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len fill && (down.[k] = k || fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (r in lo .. hi). fill.[P.at order r] = v
  requires P.done_if_upto fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen pos lo
  requires P.linked_upto down flux seen pos lo w
  requires P.ready_in down order w flux gathered lo hi
  requires P.ready_vals fill down acc order bed0 gathered newbed newout lo hi
  ensures P.done_if_upto fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen pos hi
  ensures P.linked_upto down flux seen pos hi w
=
  spread q in lo .. hi @owns(bed, pos) @owns(flux, pos) @owns(seen, pos)
    ensures seen.[order.[q]] = gathered.[q] && bed.[order.[q]] = newbed.[q] && flux.[order.[q]] = newout.[q]
  do
    let c = order.[q] in
    seen.[c] <- gathered.[q];
    bed.[c] <- newbed.[q];
    flux.[c] <- newout.[q]
  done;
  committed fill down acc order pos w bed0 gathered newbed newout (old bed) (old flux) (old seen) bed flux seen lo hi v

docs.title: 5. The step, as one command buffer
docs.text:
The waves of a step are found first, on the CPU. A wave is a run of positions of one height, so the scan writes where each one starts:

let spec wave_at (fill : [u16]) (order : [usize]) (lo : usize) (hi : usize) : bool @opaque
  requires len order = len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len fill
= lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  && (forall (r in lo .. hi). fill.[P.at order r] = fill.[P.at order lo])

let lemma use_wave (fill : [u16]) (order : [usize]) (lo : usize) (hi : usize) : unit
  requires len order = len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len fill
  requires wave_at fill order lo hi
  ensures lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  ensures forall (r in lo .. hi). fill.[P.at order r] = fill.[P.at order lo]
  with wave_at
= ()

let lemma close_wave (fill : [u16]) (order : [usize]) (lo : usize) (hi : usize) : unit
  requires len order = len fill
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len fill
  requires lo < hi && hi <= len fill
  requires forall (r in lo .. hi). fill.[P.at order r] = fill.[P.at order lo]
  ensures wave_at fill order lo hi
  with wave_at
= ()

let wave_starts (fill : [u16]) (order : [usize]) (starts : borrowed inout mutable [usize]) : usize
  requires len order = len fill && len starts = len fill + 1 && len fill > 0
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len fill
  ensures 1 <= result && result <= len fill
  ensures starts.[0] = 0 && starts.[result] = len fill
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. result). wave_at fill order (starts.[k]) (starts.[k + 1])
=
  starts.[0] <- 0;
  let m : mutable usize = 0 in
  for r in 1 .. len fill
    invariant m < r && starts.[0] = 0 && starts.[m] < r
    invariant forall (t in starts.[m] .. r). fill.[P.at order t] = fill.[P.at order (starts.[m])]
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. m). wave_at fill order (starts.[k]) (starts.[k + 1])
  do
    if fill.[order.[r]] <> fill.[order.[r - 1]] then (
      let lo = starts.[m] in
      close_wave fill order lo r;
      starts.[m + 1] <- r;
      m <- m + 1
    ) else ()
  done;
  let lo = starts.[m] in
  close_wave fill order lo (len fill);
  starts.[m + 1] <- len fill;
  m + 1

The mass the step sends off the map is the outlets' loads, added in height order, after the step:

let out_sum (order : [usize]) (down : [usize]) (flux : [u32]) : u64
  requires len down = len order && len flux = len order && len order < max u32
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len order
  ensures result = P.osum order down flux (len order)
=
  let s : mutable u64 = 0 in
  for q in 0 .. len order
    invariant s = P.osum order down flux q
  do
    P.osum_next order down flux q;
    let c = order.[q] in
    let t : u32 = if down.[c] = c then flux.[c] else 0 in
    s <- s + t
  done;
  s

Then the step is one sequential for over the waves with @place(gpu) on it (ADR 0068, section 9). Each iteration's two spreads, which piac finds through the calls of wave and commit, become two dispatches. The host runs the rest of the body as it encodes them: it reads the bounds from starts, which no kernel writes, and the lemma calls leave no code. So the whole step is one command buffer, with the buffers wrapped once and one wait. Its invariants are the ones pull_step keeps, so on Ok its postcondition is pull_step's.

let pull_step_on_gpu (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (w : usize) (bed0 : [u32])
    (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (flux : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (seen : borrowed inout mutable [u64])
    (gathered : borrowed inout mutable [u64]) (newbed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (newout : borrowed inout mutable [u32])
    (starts : borrowed inout mutable [usize]) (gone : u64) : result u64 gpu_error
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len bed0 = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len flux = len fill && len seen = len fill
  requires len gathered = len fill && len newbed = len fill && len newout = len fill && len starts = len fill + 1
  requires w >= 3 && w < max usize && len fill < max u32 && gone <= max u32
  requires forall (r in 0 .. len order). order.[r] < len pos && pos.[order.[r]] = r
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] = k || (down.[k] < len fill && fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len fill
  ensures (match result with
           | Ok s -> P.settled_if fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen && P.linked down flux seen w
                     && s = gone + P.osum order down flux (len fill)
           | Err _ -> true)
=
  P.start_pull fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen pos w;
  if len fill = 0 then (P.finish_pull fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen pos w; Ok gone)
  else (
    let waves = wave_starts fill order starts in
    let run =
      for k in 0 .. waves @place(gpu)
        invariant P.done_if_upto fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen pos (starts.[k])
        invariant P.linked_upto down flux seen pos (starts.[k]) w
      do
        let lo = starts.[k] in
        let hi = starts.[k + 1] in
        use_wave fill order lo hi;
        wave fill down acc order w bed0 flux lo hi gathered newbed newout;
        P.ready_init fill down acc order w bed0 flux gathered newbed newout lo hi;
        commit fill down acc order pos w bed0 gathered newbed newout bed flux seen lo hi (fill.[order.[lo]])
      done
    in
    match run with
    | Ok -> (P.finish_pull fill down acc bed0 bed flux seen pos w; Ok (gone + out_sum order down flux))
    | Err e -> Err e)

Its C entry point: 0 with the mass sent off the map in sent.[0], or 1 plus the gpu_error, in its order. starts is scratch, one more than the cells.

let pull_step_gpu (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (w : usize) (bed0 : [u32])
    (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (flux : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (seen : borrowed inout mutable [u64])
    (gathered : borrowed inout mutable [u64]) (newbed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (newout : borrowed inout mutable [u32])
    (starts : borrowed inout mutable [usize]) (gone : u64) (sent : out mutable [u64]) : i32
=
  match pull_step_on_gpu fill down acc order pos w bed0 bed flux seen gathered newbed newout starts gone with
  | Ok s -> (sent.[0] <- s; 0)
  | Err e ->
    (match e with
     | Gpu_unavailable -> 1
     | Gpu_out_of_memory -> 2
     | Gpu_fault -> 3
     | Gpu_timeout -> 4)

docs.title: How fast it is
docs.text:
With a dispatch per wave and a command buffer for each, the step was correct but slow. On the whole tile N46E008 (3601 × 3601 cells, 3,924 waves a step), each step took 33 to 57 s against 0.5 s on the CPU. Nearly all of that time went to wrapping buffers and waiting for each command buffer. The placed sequence on this page pays those costs once a step: it binds each buffer once, and it encodes two dispatches per wave in one command buffer.

Here are three runs of srtm_gpu on N46E008, on an Apple M3 iMac, taken 2026-11-27. Times are warm, and the first run is in brackets:

Run D8, CPU / GPU Render, CPU / GPU Pull per step, CPU / GPU Wall 1 41.8 / 16.4 ms (54.0) 26.2 / 14.1 ms (19.4) 530.5 / 237.2 ms (271.8) 55.4 s 2 41.6 / 5.2 ms (37.4) 35.4 / 8.8 ms (41.3) 525.7 / 238.0 ms (261.6) 55.0 s 3 41.2 / 5.2 ms (50.1) 28.0 / 8.3 ms (22.2) 545.8 / 235.1 ms (255.7) 54.9 s

The pull step now runs on the GPU in about 236 ms, 2.2 times faster than on the CPU. Each run makes 4 steps of 3,924 waves, which is 31,392 dispatches in sequences. It wraps 58 buffers in place, and copies 16 of them (120 bytes in all). In every run, D8, render and pull match the CPU on every cell, and both send 2,861,964 out of the map.

docs.title: What is proved, and what is checked
docs.text: Claim Where When the sequence returns Ok, the GPU step is settled and linked, and sends the outlets' sum off the map pull_step_on_gpu So it is the sequential step, cell for cell same_step in pull.pia.md, whose premises these are Each thread writes only its own slots the ownership check of ADR 0060 A thread computes each cell's inflow, bed and load as the specification says gather, bed_after, load_after, in the spread's ensures Every index is in bounds and nothing overflows every function The toolchain from SPIR-V to Metal keeps the kernel's meaning srtm_gpu, a differential test against pull_step (ADR 0068, section 6)

docs.title: Debugging C++ with the REPL
docs.text:
The REPL can answer questions about code that isn't written in Pia yet. To find out whether a piece of C++ is correct, port it into a session one function at a time, try to prove it, and let each counterexample tell you what to look at next. Nothing is built: there's no piac run, no object file and no link, only cells.

This page follows such a session as Claude ran it, using the REPL's MCP server. Each step shows what Claude meant to try (Claude:), the cell it sent with the execute tool (→), the result the server sent back (←), and what Claude made of the result before the next call.

docs.title: The suspect
docs.text:
A parser reads a little-endian length-prefixed field. A caller finds the field through an offset stored in the file's header:

// Copies the field at `pos` to `out` and returns the position after it,
// or 0 on malformed input.
size_t read_field(const uint8_t* buf, size_t n, size_t pos,
                  uint8_t* out, size_t cap) {
  if (pos + 2 > n) return 0;
  size_t len = buf[pos] | (buf[pos + 1] << 8);
  if (pos + 2 + len > n) return 0;
  if (len > cap) return 0;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < len; ++i) out[i] = buf[pos + 2 + i];
  return pos + 2 + len;
}

// The name field's offset is in the first 4 bytes of the file.
size_t read_name(const uint8_t* buf, size_t n, uint8_t* out, size_t cap) {
  if (n < 4) return 0;
  uint32_t off = buf[0] | buf[1] << 8 | buf[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)buf[3] << 24;
  return read_field(buf, n, off, out, cap);
}

Every access is behind a bounds check, and the checks look right. The question is whether they are.

The port is direct. A pointer and its length become a slice: buf, n is buf : [u8], and out, cap is dst : out mutable [u8]. size_t is usize. The difference that matters is overflow. C++ wraps size_t arithmetic silently, but Pia must prove that every + doesn't overflow. So a wraparound shows up as a failed obligation, with the values that cause it.

docs.title: The session
docs.text:
On the wire, a call is an ordinary MCP tools/call, and the result is the REPL's text:

{"name": "execute", "arguments": {"code": "let read_field (buf : [u8]) (pos : usize) ..."}}

{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "[1]:2:10: failed: '+' does not overflow usize\n  counterexample: ..."}], "isError": true}

The steps below show the same calls with the code and the text laid out for reading. [n] in a result is the cell's number, and [n]:line:col is a place in that cell.

docs.title: 1. A literal port
docs.text:
Claude: I start with read_field alone, ported line for line, and send it as one cell.

→ execute

let read_field (buf : [u8]) (pos : usize) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : usize =
  if pos + 2 > len buf then 0
  else (
    let size : usize = buf.[pos] | (buf.[pos + 1] << 8) in
    if pos + 2 + size > len buf then 0
    else if size > len dst then 0
    else (
      for i in 0 .. size do dst.[i] <- buf.[pos + 2 + i] done;
      pos + 2 + size))

← result (isError)

[1]:2:10: failed: '+' does not overflow usize
  counterexample: len buf = 0, pos = 18446744073709551614, len dst = 0, result = 18446744073709551616
[1]:4:51: failed: the shift amount is less than 8
  counterexample: len buf = 4393147680799327043, pos = 2087023196055266900, len dst = 0, amount = 8
[1]: error: 2 obligations failed; nothing was committed

Claude: Two failures, and they are different kinds of failure.

The second is my mistake, not the C++'s. C++ promotes buf[pos + 1] to int before it shifts, but in my port the shift happens at u8. I'll put the shift first so that it is typed at usize, the type the result is declared with.

The first is worth taking seriously. pos = 2^64 - 2 makes pos + 2 overflow. In C++ that sum silently wraps to 0, so the check 0 > n is false and buf[pos] reads far outside the buffer.

docs.title: 2. Fix the port
docs.text:
Claude: Same function, with the shift written so that it happens at usize:

→ execute

let read_field (buf : [u8]) (pos : usize) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : usize =
  if pos + 2 > len buf then 0
  else (
    let size : usize = (buf.[pos + 1] << 8) | buf.[pos] in
    if pos + 2 + size > len buf then 0
    else if size > len dst then 0
    else (
      for i in 0 .. size do dst.[i] <- buf.[pos + 2 + i] done;
      pos + 2 + size))

← result (isError)

[2]:2:10: failed: '+' does not overflow usize
  counterexample: len buf = 0, pos = 18446744073709551614, len dst = 0, result = 18446744073709551616
[2]:5:16: failed: '+' does not overflow usize
  counterexample: len buf = 18446744073709551615, pos = 18446744073709486081, len dst = 0, result = 18446744073709551618
[2]: error: 2 obligations failed; nothing was committed

Claude: The shift is gone, and what's left are two overflows of pos + 2. They only matter if a caller can pass a pos that large, so the question is what read_field assumes about its callers. The usual contract for a function like this is that pos is somewhere inside the buffer. I'll state that as a precondition and see what's left.

docs.title: 3. Assume pos <= n
docs.text:
Claude: I add requires pos <= len buf. The body is unchanged:

→ execute

let read_field (buf : [u8]) (pos : usize) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : usize
  requires pos <= len buf
= if pos + 2 > len buf then 0
  else (
    let size : usize = (buf.[pos + 1] << 8) | buf.[pos] in
    if pos + 2 + size > len buf then 0
    else if size > len dst then 0
    else (
      for i in 0 .. size do dst.[i] <- buf.[pos + 2 + i] done;
      pos + 2 + size))

← result (isError)

[3]:3:10: failed: '+' does not overflow usize
  counterexample: len buf = 18446744073709551614, pos = 18446744073709551614, len dst = 0, result = 18446744073709551616
[3]:6:16: failed: '+' does not overflow usize
  counterexample: len buf = 18446744073709546496, pos = 18446744073709543167, len dst = 0, result = 18446744073709577512
[3]: error: 2 obligations failed; nothing was committed

Claude: Better. Every counterexample now needs a buffer within a few kilobytes of 2^64 bytes, which no real program has. C++ promises as much: no object is larger than PTRDIFF_MAX, which is 2^63 - 1 on a 64-bit target. That is a fact about the platform, not a guess, so I'll state it too.

docs.title: 4. Add the object size limit
docs.text:
Claude: A second precondition, len buf <= PTRDIFF_MAX:

→ execute

let read_field (buf : [u8]) (pos : usize) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : usize
  requires len buf <= 9223372036854775807
  requires pos <= len buf
= if pos + 2 > len buf then 0
  else (
    let size : usize = (buf.[pos + 1] << 8) | buf.[pos] in
    if pos + 2 + size > len buf then 0
    else if size > len dst then 0
    else (
      for i in 0 .. size do dst.[i] <- buf.[pos + 2 + i] done;
      pos + 2 + size))

← result

read_field : (buf : [u8]) -> (pos : usize) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> usize  (* 15 proved *)

Claude: Proved, all 15 obligations. So the C++ read_field is correct for every caller that keeps pos <= n. The next question is whether the real caller does that.

docs.title: 5. Port the caller
docs.text:
Claude: read_name takes the offset from the first four bytes of the file:

→ execute

let read_name (buf : [u8]) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : usize
  requires len buf <= 9223372036854775807
= if len buf < 4 then 0
  else (
    let off : usize = (buf.[3] << 24) | (buf.[2] << 16) | (buf.[1] << 8) | buf.[0] in
    read_field buf off dst)

← result (isError)

[5]:6:5: failed: the precondition of 'read_field' holds
  counterexample: len buf = 8190, len dst = 0
[5]: error: 1 obligation failed; nothing was committed

Claude: It doesn't. The offset comes from the file, so an 8 KB file can name any offset up to 4 GB, and read_field's precondition fails. That alone doesn't make the C++ wrong, though. pos <= n was my guess at a contract, not something the code needs. What the caller really guarantees is that pos fits in 32 bits. I'll ask whether the unchanged body is safe under that guarantee instead.

docs.title: 6. Ask about the caller's real guarantee
docs.text:
Claude: :redef replaces read_field with the same body and the precondition pos <= 2^32 - 1:

→ execute

:redef let read_field (buf : [u8]) (pos : usize) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : usize
  requires len buf <= 9223372036854775807
  requires pos <= 4294967295
= if pos + 2 > len buf then 0
  else (
    let size : usize = (buf.[pos + 1] << 8) | buf.[pos] in
    if pos + 2 + size > len buf then 0
    else if size > len dst then 0
    else (
      for i in 0 .. size do dst.[i] <- buf.[pos + 2 + i] done;
      pos + 2 + size))

← result

read_field : (buf : [u8]) -> (pos : usize) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> usize  (redefined)  (* 15 proved *)

Claude: The unchanged body is proved under that precondition too. Now I'll send the caller again.

docs.title: 7. Try the caller again
docs.text:
Claude: The same read_name as before:

→ execute

let read_name (buf : [u8]) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : usize
  requires len buf <= 9223372036854775807
= if len buf < 4 then 0
  else (
    let off : usize = (buf.[3] << 24) | (buf.[2] << 16) | (buf.[1] << 8) | buf.[0] in
    read_field buf off dst)

← result

read_name : (buf : [u8]) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> usize  (* 15 proved *)

Claude: Proved. So on a 64-bit target the original C++ is safe. A 32-bit offset plus 2 can't wrap a 64-bit size_t, so an offset past the end of the file fails the first check and read_field returns 0.

That argument depends on size_t being wider than the offset. On a 32-bit target it isn't, so I'll check that case next.

docs.title: 8. A 32-bit size_t
docs.text:
Claude: The same code with u32 in place of size_t, and the 32-bit PTRDIFF_MAX:

→ execute

let read_field32 (buf : [u8]) (pos : u32) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : u32
  requires len buf <= 2147483647
= let n : u32 = len buf in
  if pos + 2 > n then 0
  else (
    let size : u32 = (buf.[pos + 1] << 8) | buf.[pos] in
    if pos + 2 + size > n then 0
    else if size > len dst then 0
    else (
      for i in 0 .. size do dst.[i] <- buf.[pos + 2 + i] done;
      pos + 2 + size))

← result (isError)

[8]:4:10: failed: '+' does not overflow u32
  counterexample: len buf = 0, pos = 4294967294, len dst = 0, result = 4294967296
[8]: error: 1 obligation failed; nothing was committed

Claude: That's the bug. On a 32-bit build, a file whose header says 0xFFFFFFFE makes pos + 2 wrap to 0. The check passes, and buf[0xFFFFFFFE] is read: an out-of-bounds read controlled by the file.

The fix is to compare against what's left of the buffer instead of adding to pos. n - pos can't wrap once pos <= n has been checked.

docs.title: 9. Fix it for 32 bits
docs.text:
Claude: The rewritten checks, with no precondition on pos at all:

→ execute

let read_field32 (buf : [u8]) (pos : u32) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : u32
  requires len buf <= 2147483647
= let n : u32 = len buf in
  if pos > n then 0
  else if n - pos < 2 then 0
  else (
    let size : u32 = (buf.[pos + 1] << 8) | buf.[pos] in
    if size > n - pos - 2 then 0
    else if size > len dst then 0
    else (
      for i in 0 .. size do dst.[i] <- buf.[pos + 2 + i] done;
      pos + 2 + size))

← result

read_field32 : (buf : [u8]) -> (pos : u32) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> u32  (* 17 proved *)

Claude: Proved. Now the same fix in the 64-bit version, which read_name already calls.

docs.title: 10. Fix it for 64 bits
docs.text:
Claude: :redef again, this time with no preconditions. I also add an ensures that the position returned is never past the end of the buffer:

→ execute

:redef let read_field (buf : [u8]) (pos : usize) (dst : out mutable [u8]) : usize
  ensures result = 0 || result <= len buf
= if pos > len buf then 0
  else if len buf - pos < 2 then 0
  else (
    let size : usize = (buf.[pos + 1] << 8) | buf.[pos] in
    if size > len buf - pos - 2 then 0
    else if size > len dst then 0
    else (
      for i in 0 .. size do dst.[i] <- buf.[pos + 2 + i] done;
      pos + 2 + size))

← result

read_field : (buf : [u8]) -> (pos : usize) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> usize  (redefined)  (* 16 proved *)

Claude: Proved, and with no assumption at all, not even the object size limit. :redef also proves everything that uses read_field again, so read_name still holds against the fixed version. Its call needs no change.

docs.title: 11. Check the environment
docs.text:
Claude: Last, I list the environment to see what the session ended with:

→ execute

:env

← result

[7] let read_name : (buf : [u8]) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> usize
[9] let read_field32 : (buf : [u8]) -> (pos : u32) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> u32
[10] let read_field : (buf : [u8]) -> (pos : usize) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> usize

Claude: The fixed read_field from cell 10, the 32-bit version, and read_name, all proved together.

docs.title: The verdict
docs.text:
read_field is correct whenever pos <= n, and read_name breaks that contract. On 64-bit targets that's harmless. On 32-bit targets it's an out-of-bounds read that the file controls. The fix, in C++:

if (pos > n || n - pos < 2) return 0;
size_t len = buf[pos] | (buf[pos + 1] << 8);
if (len > n - pos - 2 || len > cap) return 0;

This is proved for both widths, with no assumptions about pos.

docs.title: What the REPL adds
docs.text:
• Assumptions are explicit and cheap to change. Each assumption (pos <= n, the object size limit, pos < 2^32) went in as a precondition in a cell of its own. Each counterexample showed which one was missing, and a wrong guess cost one cell.
  • :redef answers "who relies on this?". Changing read_field's contract proved read_name again against it. That's how "safe on 64-bit, unsafe on 32-bit" was settled instead of argued.
  • Read each failure against the source language's rules. The REPL reports a mistake in the port (the u8 shift) the same way as a bug in the original. C++ promotes small integers before it shifts, but it really does wrap size_t, so only the overflow is a finding.
