docs.title: The REPL
docs.text:
pia repl is an interactive Pia session. Each definition you enter joins a persistent environment, as in a Lisp REPL, and later input can use it, ask about it and redefine it. Nothing is relaxed for interactive use: a definition joins the environment only when every proof obligation in the whole environment is proved, and an expression is proved before it is compiled and run. The design is ADR 0031.

Build it with:

bazel build //tools/pia
alias pia="$PWD/bazel-bin/tools/pia/pia"

docs.title: A session
docs.text:
let sum (a : u8) (b : u8) : u16
  ensures result >= a
= a + b
sum 200 100
let limit : u8 = 200
let bump (a : u8) : u8 = a + 1
let bump (a : u8) : u8 requires a < 255 = a + 1
let bump (a : u8) : u8 requires a < 200 = a + 1
:redef let bump (a : u8) : u8 requires a < 200 = a + 1
bump 41
bump 250
:type sum 1 2
:env

Each cell is proved first. bump in cell 4 can overflow, so it is refused with a counterexample, and cell 5 adds the precondition that rules it out. Cell 6 tries to define bump again, which the no-shadowing rule forbids, so cell 7 replaces it with :redef. Calling bump 250 fails its precondition at compile time, so it never runs:

$ pia repl < session.pia
sum : (a : u8) -> (b : u8) -> u16  (* 2 proved *)
- : u16 = 300
limit : u8 = 200
[4]:1:28: failed: '+' does not overflow u8
  counterexample: a = 255, result = 256
[4]: error: 1 obligation failed; nothing was committed
bump : (a : u8) -> u8  (* 1 proved *)
[6]:1:1: error: 'bump' is already defined in cell [5]; Pia does not allow shadowing (ADR 0022), so name it bump' or replace it with :redef
bump : (a : u8) -> u8  (redefined)  (* 1 proved *)
- : u8 = 42
[9]:1:1: failed: the precondition of 'bump' holds
[9]: error: 1 obligation failed; nothing was committed
sum 1 2 : u16
[1] let sum : (a : u8) -> (b : u8) -> u16
[3] let limit : u8
[7] let bump : (a : u8) -> u8

On a terminal, pia repl prints a banner and reads cells with a line editor: arrows and the usual Emacs keys move and edit, Up and Down step through the history (kept in ~/.pia_history), and Ctrl-D leaves.

docs.title: Cells
docs.text:
A cell is one input: Pia code, or a command that starts with :. Code can hold several top-level items. A definition goes on to the next line until its =, so a header can be followed by its contracts on the lines below, and a cell also goes on while a bracket, a comment, a string or a quote is open, or while the last line ends with a token that needs more, such as an operator, then or in. On a terminal an empty line ends a cell early. On a pipe, a cell ends where the next line starts at column 1.

Each cell is checked together with the environment, as one program:

  • Definitions (let, types, let meta metaprograms and operators) join the environment if everything verifies. A constant's value is shown with its type.
  • Expressions are evaluated. Any expression can start at column 1, such as 1 + 2, on its own or after a definition in the same cell; in a file only a metaprogram's call can. A line that starts with - at column 1 starts a new expression too, so a subtraction that goes on to the next line indents it. Each one becomes a hidden constant that is verified like any definition, so a call outside a precondition fails before anything runs. It is then compiled for the host with the ORC JIT and run, and its value is shown as - : type = value. Expressions do not join the environment.
  • Metaprograms run as they do in a file: operators declared in earlier cells apply to later ones, @derive(eq) adds its functions, and a top-level call of a let meta function adds the items it returns.

A cell is a transaction. If any obligation fails, or is not proved and not accepted with :allow, nothing in the cell is committed, and the failures are shown with their counterexamples. So the environment is always a program that verifies.

Locations are written [cell]:line:col, counting lines within the cell.

docs.title: Redefinition
docs.text:
Pia has no shadowing (ADR 0022), and the REPL keeps that rule: defining a name that already exists is an error that suggests a primed name such as bump'. To replace a definition, use :redef. The new definition is checked in place of the old one together with everything else, so each definition that uses it is proved again against the new one. If any of those proofs breaks, the redefinition is refused, and nothing changes.

:forget name removes a definition the same way. It is refused while anything still uses it.

A name that a metaprogram call generated belongs to that call: redefine the call instead.

docs.title: Live redefinition
docs.text:
:spawn <expr> proves an expression, then runs it on a thread of its own, so the session carries on while it runs. Redefining a function the task uses swaps the new code into the running task, as in Lisp, as long as the change is proved safe for code that is already running (ADR 0031):

  • Every definition is called through a slot. In the REPL, a call from one definition to another loads the callee's current code from its slot. Committing a redefinition stores the new code in the slot, so each call that starts afterwards runs it, while calls already running finish on the code they started in. The engine holding old code stays alive until no task uses it.
  • A refinement swaps at once. The task's code was proved against the old definition's contract. So the new definition's body is proved against that old contract as well as its own, as a hidden function: its obligations under the old requires, and the old ensures. If that proof holds and the type is unchanged, the swap is safe for the running task wherever it is, and the result says swapped into running task 1.
  • Any other change swaps together with its callers. If the new body does not meet the old contract, or its type changed (also when a record type it uses changed), the code that calls it was proved against something that no longer holds. The redefinition and everything that uses it are verified again, as always, and then the changed definition and every definition that calls it are swapped together, at a moment when no task is running any of them. Calls into that set from outside it wait while the set drains, for at most two seconds. Their callers outside the set relied only on contracts that did not change, so they carry on. If a task never leaves the set, for example because its own expression calls a definition in it, nothing is committed until the task finishes.
  • Everything else is the same as without tasks. Definitions no running task can reach change freely. :forget and :reset wait for the tasks that need what they would remove.

To find that moment, code that a task may run counts its calls in progress, one counter per definition. That costs a few nanoseconds per call, so the REPL counts only in code compiled while a task runs or for :spawn. Compiled programs never count.

let step (a : u64) : u64
  requires a < 1000
  ensures result = 1
= 1
let total (n : u64) : u64
  requires n <= 8000000000
= let s : mutable u64 = 0 in
  for i in 0 .. n
    invariant s <= 2 * i
  do s <- s + step 5 done;
  s
:spawn total 1000000000
:redef let step (a : u64) : u64 requires a < 1000 ensures result = 1 = 2 - 1
:redef let step (a : u64) : u64 requires a < 1000 ensures result <= 2 = 2
:wait 1

$ pia repl < live.pia
step : (a : usize) -> usize  (* 1 proved *)
total : (n : usize) -> usize  (* 4 proved *)
task 1 (total 1000000000) running
step : (a : usize) -> usize  (redefined, swapped into running task 1)  (* 2 proved *)
[5]: error: 'step' no longer refines what running code was proved against (the new body does not meet the old contract: the postcondition holds (the old contract at [4]:1:44)), so it can only be swapped together with 'total', which calls it, at a moment when no task is running any of them, but task 1 stayed inside 'total' for 2000 ms; nothing was committed (wait for the task with :wait)
task 1 (total 1000000000) done: usize = 1000000000

The second step would still let total verify, but total was proved against result = 1, and the task never leaves total, so the change waits for it. With one more level of calls, the same change goes through while the task runs:

let chunk (k : u64) : u64
  requires k <= 1000
  ensures result <= 2 * k
= let s : mutable u64 = 0 in
  for i in 0 .. k
    invariant s <= 2 * i
  do s <- s + step 5 done;
  s
let many (n : u64) : u64
  requires n <= 8000000
= let s : mutable u64 = 0 in
  for i in 0 .. n
    invariant s <= 2000 * i
  do s <- s + chunk 1000 done;
  s
:spawn many 1000000
:redef let step (a : u64) : u64 requires a < 1000 ensures result <= 2 = 2
:wait 2

task 2 (many 1000000) running
step : (a : usize) -> usize  (redefined, swapped into running task 2 at a moment when no task was running 'chunk' or 'step')  (* 1 proved *)
task 2 (many 1000000) done: usize = 1497312000

chunk still verifies with the new step, and many relies only on chunk's contract, which did not change. So step and chunk are swapped together between two calls of chunk. Every call of chunk ran wholly on the old code or wholly on the new, which is why the value is a multiple of 1000.

docs.title: Metaprograms that change the environment
docs.text:
The REPL gives metaprograms the environment as data, through Pia.Live: listing () lists every definition, and redefine x turns the definitions in the syntax x into replacements (metaprograms). A metaprogram's changes take exactly the same path as a :redef cell, so nothing it does can install code that is not proved, and a definition a running task uses is swapped in only if it refines the old one:

let meta faster () =
  redefine `( let step ($!a : u64) : u64 requires $!a < 1000 ensures $!result = 1 = 1 + 0 )

Pia.Live exists only in the REPL. piac refuses redefine, and compiled programs call functions directly, with no slots.

docs.title: State
docs.text:
A let with no parameters whose type says mutable is a state: a value that persists from cell to cell, which definitions can read and change (ADR 0031). Its invariant is a fact that every definition must keep:

let count : mutable u8
  invariant count <= 100
= 0
let bump () : unit = if count < 100 then count <- count + 1 else ()
bump ()
bump ()
count
let tick () : unit = count <- count + 1
:redef let count : mutable u16 invariant count <= 1000 = old count * 10
count

$ pia repl < state.pia
count : mutable u8 = 0  (* 1 proved *)
bump : () -> unit  (* 5 proved *)
- : unit = ()
- : unit = ()
- : u8 = 2
[1]:2:19: failed: the postcondition holds
[6]: error: 1 obligation failed; nothing was committed
count : mutable u16 = 20  (redefined, migrated from mutable u8)  (* 3 proved *)
- : u16 = 20

tick could take count past 100, so it is refused, and the failure points at the invariant it would break.

  • How it is proved. Every definition that uses a state, directly or through a call, takes it as a borrowed inout mutable one-element buffer, so the verifier treats it like any other buffer. Each such definition requires the invariant and ensures it, every loop in it has the invariant as a loop invariant, and a definition that never writes the state ensures it is unchanged. The initial value is proved to meet the invariant. Since an invariant holds whenever no call is in progress, a redefinition of a function that uses a state keeps the invariant too: its contract includes it.
  • Migration. :redef of a state starts it again from its new initial value, unless the value names old count, the value of the definition it replaces. Then the new value is computed from the old one, and proved to meet the new type and the new invariant for every old value the old invariant allows. Above, old count * 10 fits in u16 and stays at most 1000 because the old count is at most 100. Going back to u8 with old count would be refused, since old count may be 1000.
  • Tasks. A state that a running task uses belongs to the task until it finishes. Reading it, writing it, redefining it or forgetting it waits for the task, so a task and the session never race on it. Functions that use it can still be redefined while the task runs, as above: a new body that keeps the old contract, and with it the invariant, is swapped into the task.
  • Cells. A cell can be a statement, such as count <- 7, and its result is checked against the invariant like any definition's.

A state is an integer or a bool for now. State belongs to the REPL until modules (M8) bring module state to compiled programs, so piac refuses an invariant on a definition.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command :type <expr> the type of an expression, or of a definition :proof [<name>] a definition's obligations and how each was proved, or a summary of all of them :env the environment's definitions, with the cell each came from :source <name> a definition's source :redef <code> replace the definitions of the names code defines :forget <name> remove a definition that nothing uses :allow [<spec>] accept unproved obligations in a function, or at [cell]:line[:col]; with no argument, list what is accepted :spawn <expr> run an expression as a background task (see Live redefinition) :tasks the tasks, running or done, with their values :wait <n> wait for task n to finish, and show its value :load <file> run a file as one cell; for a literate .pia.md file, its pia blocks :reset empty the environment :help [<topic>] the list of commands and guide topics, or one topic of the language guide (see MCP server) :quit leave

pia repl takes the same --allow-unproved=<spec> flag as piac, and --meta-cycles=N, --timeout-ms=N (the solver's limit per obligation) and --no-run (verify, but never compile or run). Files named on the command line are loaded first, each as one cell.

docs.title: JSON output
docs.text:
pia repl --json reads one JSON request per line and writes one JSON result per line, for scripts and tools. A request:

{"id": 1, "code": "let sum (a : u8) (b : u8) : u16 = a + b"}

and its result, broken over lines here:

{"cell": 1, "events": [
  {"kind": "proof", "method": "intervals", "name": "sum", "status": "proved", "text": "'+' does not overflow u16", "where": {"cell": 1, "column": 37, "line": 1}},
  {"kind": "defined", "name": "sum", "type": "(a : u8) -> (b : u8) -> u16"}], "id": 1, "ok": true}

id is copied from the request, if it has one. --input=text and --output=json mix the two: cells read as text, results written as JSON.

Each event has a kind:

Kind Fields defined, redefined name, type, value, text a definition joined the environment; value for a constant; type is type, meta or operator for those items; text says which running tasks a redefinition was swapped into removed name :forget removed it value type, value an expression's value type text, type :type's answer proof name, status, text, method, counterexample, where one obligation: status is proved, failed, unproved or allowed, text the claim, counterexample an object of names and values error text, where info text command output and notes task name, text, type, status, value a background task: name is its number, text its expression, status running or done, and value its value once done

where is {"cell", "line", "column"}. The exit status is 1 if any cell failed.

A cell that reached the verifier also has stats, what its proof took: cell_ms, verify_ms, solve_ms (wall clock, over threads solver threads) and run_ms (milliseconds); cell_goals, cell_intervals and cell_smt for the cell's own goals; goals, proved, failed, unproved, allowed and smt for the whole environment, which every cell proves again; cost, Z3's resource count; and costliest, the slowest solver goals: up to three of the cell's own, then up to three the environment re-proved, each with name, text, status, ms, cost, where and cell (true for the cell's own). The text output leaves them out, since times differ from run to run.

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text:
pia mcp serves a persistent REPL session over the Model Context Protocol (stdio transport), so an agent such as Claude can use Pia interactively. It has exactly two tools, in the style of Code Mode:

  • execute {code, wait_ms?, json?} runs a cell, code or a command, in the session. It waits up to wait_ms (10 seconds by default) and returns the cell's result as the text pia repl prints. A cell that is still running returns its job number instead.
  • poll {job, wait_ms?, json?} waits for a job and returns its state (queued, running or done) and, once it is done, its result.

With json: true, a result also carries the job, its state and the JSON result above as structured content. It is off by default because some clients, Claude Code among them, show the agent the structured content in place of the text, and the events are several times longer than the text.

A tool result is an error when the cell failed, so the agent sees failed proofs and counterexamples as errors to fix. The agent skills teach an agent how to work with it.

The server also teaches the language itself, for agents that have no skills loaded:

  • Its instructions (which clients put in the agent's context when it connects) are a primer of under 2 KB: the binding form, bounded integers, where contracts go, no shadowing, comments, and the list of guide topics.
  • :help <topic>, sent through execute, returns one section of the guide: syntax, facts, shapes, pitfalls, contracts, loops, termination, specs and more (:help lists them). The same text is served as MCP resources, pia://guide/<topic>.
  • Every result says what its proof took, after the REPL's text: the time for the cell, split into verifying (and the solver), running, and parsing and compiling; how many goals the cell raised and how each was proved, and how many the environment re-proved; and the slowest solver goals, the cell's own and the environment's apart, with their locations and Z3 resource counts.
  • A failed cell ends with hints, one line per kind of failure, such as hint: arithmetic is checked at the operands' width: ... (:help facts). They are only in the server's results, not in pia repl's output.

The guide is cut from the pia-language, pia-contracts and pia-mcp skills when the server is built (src/repl/embed_guide.py), so it says what the skills say, and their examples are proved by the skills test. To use it from Claude Code:

claude mcp add pia -- "$PWD/bazel-bin/tools/pia/pia" mcp

docs.title: Claude driving a session
docs.text:
Here is Claude using the server from Claude Code to work through the examples on these pages. Each >>> is a tool call and each <<< is its result, verbatim apart from the edge detector's list of functions, which is cut short. The server was started in the repository's root, so :load takes paths from there. A result is the same text pia repl prints, and (isError) marks a cell that failed.

>>> execute {"code": "let bump (a : u8) : u8 = a + 1"}
<<< (isError) [1]:1:28: failed: '+' does not overflow u8
  counterexample: a = 255, result = 256
[1]: error: 1 obligation failed; nothing was committed
>>> execute {"code": "let bump (a : u8) : u8 requires a < 200 ensures result = a + 1 = a + 1"}
<<< bump : (a : u8) -> u8  (* 2 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": "let double (a : u8) : u16 requires a < 100 ensures result = a + a = bump a + a - 1"}
<<< double : (a : u8) -> u16  (* 4 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": "double 41"}
<<< - : u16 = 82
>>> execute {"code": ":redef let bump (a : u8) : u8 requires a < 10 ensures result = a + 1 = a + 1"}
<<< (isError) [3]:1:69: failed: the precondition of 'bump' holds
  counterexample: a = 64
[5]: error: 1 obligation failed; the redefinition is not committed
>>> execute {"code": ":redef let bump (a : u8) : u8 requires a < 255 ensures result = a + 1 = a + 1"}
<<< bump : (a : u8) -> u8  (redefined)  (* 2 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": "let count : mutable u8\n  invariant count <= 100\n= 0"}
<<< count : mutable u8 = 0  (* 1 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": "let tick () : unit = if count < 100 then count <- count + 1 else ()"}
<<< tick : () -> unit  (* 5 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": "tick ()"}
<<< - : unit = ()
>>> execute {"code": "let tick' () : unit = count <- count + 1"}
<<< (isError) [7]:2:19: failed: the postcondition holds
[10]: error: 1 obligation failed; nothing was committed
>>> execute {"code": ":redef let count : mutable u16 invariant count <= 1000 = old count * 10"}
<<< count : mutable u16 = 10  (redefined, migrated from mutable u8)  (* 3 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": ":reset"}
<<< the environment is empty
>>> execute {"code": ":load examples/edges/edges_buggy.pia"}
<<< (isError) [13]:13:29: failed: the index is within bounds
  counterexample: len src = 2311472508747907072, w = 0, m = 2311472508747907071, index = 2311472508747907072, length = 2311472508747907072
[13]:15:31: failed: the index is within bounds
  counterexample: len src = 17329207052307791873, w = 8255452159714263041, m = 9073754892593528831, index = 17329207052307791873, length = 17329207052307791873
[13]: error: 2 obligations failed; nothing was committed
>>> execute {"code": ":load examples/edges/edges.pia"}
<<< luma : (r : u8) -> (g : u8) -> (b : u8) -> u8  (* 6 proved *)
gray : (rgb : [u8]) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> unit  (* 8 proved *)
mean_at : (src : [u8]) -> (w : usize) -> (m : usize) -> u8  (* 28 proved *)
...
edges : (rgb : [u8]) -> (w : usize) -> (luma_buf : out mutable [u8]) -> (smooth : out mutable [u8]) -> (dst : out mutable [u8]) -> unit  (* 3 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": ":reset"}
<<< the environment is empty
>>> execute {"code": ":load docs/cases/heartbleed.pia.md"}
<<< heartbeat : (req : [u8]) -> (resp : out mutable [u8]) -> usize  (* 22 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": ":load docs/cases/binary-search.pia.md"}
<<< search : (xs : [i32]) -> (key : i32) -> i32  (* 24 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": ":env"}
<<< [16] let heartbeat : (req : [u8]) -> (resp : out mutable [u8]) -> usize
[17] let search : (xs : [i32]) -> (key : i32) -> i32
>>> execute {"code": "let spin (n : u64) : u64 =\n  let i : mutable u64 = 0 in\n  while i < n\n    invariant i <= n\n    decreases n - i\n  do i <- i + 1 done;\n  i"}
<<< spin : (n : usize) -> usize  (* 4 proved *)
>>> execute {"code": ":spawn spin 3000000000"}
<<< task 1 (spin 3000000000) running
>>> execute {"code": ":wait 1"}
<<< task 1 (spin 3000000000) done: usize = 3000000000

Here is what each step shows:

  • Contracts. The first bump can overflow, so it is refused with the input that breaks it. The second adds a precondition and an ensures, and double is proved from bump's contract alone, before double 41 runs.
  • Redefinition is checked against its users. Tightening bump to a < 10 would break double, which calls it with a < 100, so the error points at that call in cell 3 and nothing changes. Loosening it to a < 255 is accepted, and double is proved again.
  • State. tick' could take count past 100, so it is refused at the invariant. The :redef of count migrates its value to u16 through old count, and the migration is proved for every value the old invariant allows.
  • Files. :load runs a file as one cell. The buggy edge detector is refused with counterexamples (the demo explains its bug), and the fixed one is proved. A literate .pia.md file runs its pia blocks, so the Heartbleed and binary search case studies load as they stand. :reset comes first because the two edge files define the same names, and Pia does not allow shadowing.
  • Tasks. :spawn returns at once, while the task runs on its own thread. A cell that takes longer than wait_ms returns a job number to poll instead.

The transcript is not checked by the documentation tests, since they cannot run an agent. Every cell's output is the REPL's text, which the sessions above are checked against.

Debugging C++ with the REPL follows a longer session, in which Claude uses the server to decide whether a piece of C++ has a bug.

docs.title: The session API
docs.text:
Every front end is a thin layer over two C++ classes in src/repl, so the planned Jupyter kernel (#64) will share them too:

  • pia::repl::Session holds the environment. execute(cell) runs one cell and returns a CellResult: its number, whether it succeeded, and its events. render turns that into the text pia repl prints and toJson into the JSON above. Session::isComplete(text) tells a front end whether a cell needs more lines.
  • pia::repl::Kernel runs a session on a worker thread. submit(cell) queues a cell and returns a job number; poll(job, wait) returns its state, and its result once it is done. Jobs run one at a time, in order.

Neither is part of the Pia runtime. Compiled programs never contain the session, the JIT or the environment.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Each cell verifies and compiles the whole environment again. That is quick for interactive sizes; caching proofs per definition is planned.
  • Values of integer, bool, unit and record types can be shown. Arrays and slices cannot be returned yet, so they cannot be shown either.
  • Everything not compiled yet is not available in the REPL either.
  • A task cannot be stopped before it finishes. Its termination is proved, but that does not bound how long it takes.
  • Swaps happen one definition at a time. A change to a group of definitions that a running task uses is accepted only if each one refines its old contract. A change to a type, or to a function's type, waits for the tasks that use it: migrating live values to a new layout is designed but not built.
  • Tasks have no I/O yet, so the only thing they produce is their value.

docs.title: Demo: sediment transport
docs.text:
The second half of the stream delineation demo moves sediment over the landscape the first half delineated (ADR 0055). Sediment is counted in whole units of mass, a u32 per cell, in three buffers: bed, the erodible sediment resting in each cell; load, what the water leaving a cell carries; and inflow, what drains into it. One more number, gone, counts what has left the map through outlets.

Each cell's water has a capacity, how much it can carry. Where it carries less, it erodes the bed, at most the whole bed; where it carries more, it deposits the excess. A step visits the cells from highest to lowest, so every cell is visited after the cells that drain into it, and each cell's load moves on to the cell below, or off the map.

The theorem is that the total never changes:

sum bed + sum load + sum inflow + gone = old (the same)

exactly, in whole units, with no tolerance. It is the postcondition of every function below, from a single write to n time steps over the whole map, and it bounds every cell, so nothing overflows.

Here is the result: three "years" of rain over the demo's 384×256 test terrain. Each year has uniform rain, then a storm band moving down the map, then a wet season and a dry one, and each frame is one epoch of 4 steps (section 6). Streams are coloured blue to orange by the sediment they carry, lakes are pale blue, and every other cell takes its watershed's tint, shaded by height. Before each epoch, the ground is the rock plus the deposited sediment, and the flow is recomputed over it. The whole animation conserves mass exactly: 7,276,468 units stay on the map and 2,553,932 leave through outlets, the 9,830,400 it started with.

The proved GIF encoder (ADR 0054) writes the animation. To make it yourself, run bazel run //examples/streams with no arguments, which writes streams-output-evolution.gif.

This page is the program, a literate Pia file like streams.pia.md and its own module, so the two prove in parallel. The C program in examples/streams calls sediment with the filled heights, the flow directions and the accumulation from the first half, and draws the result with render_load from that page.

module Sediment : Transport

interface Transport @abi(c) = sig
  let sediment : (fill : [u16]) -> (down : [usize]) -> (acc : [u32])
      -> (n : u32) -> (bed : inout mutable [u32])
      -> (load : out mutable [u32]) -> (inflow : out mutable [u32])
      -> (flux : out mutable [u32]) -> (order : out mutable [usize])
      -> (pos : out mutable [usize]) -> (cnt : out mutable [u32])
      -> (first : out mutable [usize]) -> (next : out mutable [usize])
      -> (last : out mutable [usize]) -> (owner : out mutable [u16]) -> u64
    requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill
    requires len bed = len fill && len load = len fill && len inflow = len fill
    requires len flux = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill
    requires len owner = len fill && len fill < max u32
    requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1
    requires forall (k in 0..len down).
               down.[k] = k || (down.[k] < len fill && fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  let surface : (rock : [u16]) -> (bed : [u32]) -> (height : out mutable [u16])
      -> unit
    requires len bed = len rock && len height = len rock
  let rain_uniform : (r : u8) -> (rain : out mutable [u32]) -> unit
    requires len rain <= 16'777'215
  let rain_band : (w : usize) -> (lo : usize) -> (hi : usize) -> (inside : u8)
      -> (outside : u8) -> (rain : out mutable [u32]) -> unit
    requires w > 0 && len rain <= 16'777'215
  let rain_season : (wet : bool) -> (r : u8) -> (rain : out mutable [u32]) -> unit
    requires len rain <= 16'777'215
  let drainage : (fill : [u16]) -> (down : [usize]) -> (acc : out mutable [u32])
      -> (basin : out mutable [usize]) -> (rain : out mutable [u32])
      -> (pend : out mutable [u32]) -> (order : out mutable [usize])
      -> (pos : out mutable [usize]) -> (cnt : out mutable [u32])
      -> (first : out mutable [usize]) -> (next : out mutable [usize])
      -> (last : out mutable [usize]) -> (owner : out mutable [u16]) -> unit
    requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len basin = len fill
    requires len rain = len fill && len pend = len fill
    requires len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len owner = len fill
    requires len fill < max u32
    requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1
    requires forall (j in 0..len down).
               down.[j] = j || (down.[j] < len fill && fill.[down.[j]] < fill.[j])
  let evolve : (fill : [u16]) -> (down : [usize]) -> (rain : [u32]) -> (k : u32)
      -> (bed : inout mutable [u32]) -> (load : inout mutable [u32])
      -> (inflow : inout mutable [u32]) -> (flux : out mutable [u32])
      -> (flow : out mutable [u32]) -> (pend : out mutable [u32])
      -> (order : out mutable [usize]) -> (pos : out mutable [usize])
      -> (cnt : out mutable [u32]) -> (first : out mutable [usize])
      -> (next : out mutable [usize]) -> (last : out mutable [usize])
      -> (owner : out mutable [u16]) -> u64
    requires len down = len fill && len rain = len fill
    requires len bed = len fill && len load = len fill && len inflow = len fill
    requires len flux = len fill && len flow = len fill && len pend = len fill
    requires len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len owner = len fill
    requires len fill < max u32
    requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1
    requires forall (j in 0..len down).
               down.[j] = j || (down.[j] < len fill && fill.[down.[j]] < fill.[j])
end

docs.title: 1. The sum and the point update
docs.text:
let spec elt (xs : [u32]) (i : usize) : u32
  requires i < len xs
= xs.[i]

sum xs n is the sum of xs.[0 .. n], a u64. An element is read through elt, whose u32 result type tells the solver the element's range each time sum unfolds. The bound in the ensures keeps the u64 from overflowing; it is the one product in this stage, and it widens the encoding only for the functions that use sum (docs/verifier.md, "Encoding").

let spec sum (xs : [u32]) (n : usize) : u64
  requires n <= len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  ensures result <= (max u32 + 1) * n
  decreases n
= if n = 0 then 0 else sum xs (n - 1) + elt xs (n - 1)

The lemmas about sum are proved by induction. Each inductive step goes through one of three small lemmas with no quantifier in sight: with a forall among the facts, the solver does not find the one-step unfolding by itself.

let lemma step (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (n : usize) : unit
  requires 0 < n && n <= len xs && n <= len ys && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires sum ys (n - 1) = sum xs (n - 1) && ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]
  ensures sum ys n = sum xs n
= ()

let lemma step_after (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (i : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires i < n - 1 && n <= len xs && n <= len ys && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires sum ys (n - 1) + xs.[i] = sum xs (n - 1) + ys.[i] && ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]
  ensures sum ys n + xs.[i] = sum xs n + ys.[i]
= ()

let lemma step_at (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (i : usize) : unit
  requires i < len xs && i < len ys && i < max u32 + 1
  requires sum ys i = sum xs i
  ensures sum ys (i + 1) + xs.[i] = sum xs (i + 1) + ys.[i]
= ()

If ys is xs except at i, the prefixes before i have the same sum.

let lemma frame (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (i : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires len xs = len ys && n <= i && i < len xs && len xs <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len xs). k <> i ==> ys.[k] = xs.[k]
  ensures sum ys n = sum xs n
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then (frame xs ys i (n - 1); assert ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]; step xs ys n)

The point update: writing ys.[i] in place of xs.[i] changes the sum of every prefix that holds i by ys.[i] - xs.[i]. Every move of sediment is a pair of such writes.

let lemma update (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (i : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires len xs = len ys && i < n && n <= len xs && len xs <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len xs). k <> i ==> ys.[k] = xs.[k]
  ensures sum ys n + xs.[i] = sum xs n + ys.[i]
  decreases n
= if n > i + 1 then (update xs ys i (n - 1); assert ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]; step_after xs ys i n)
  else (frame xs ys i i; step_at xs ys i; assert n = i + 1)

let lemma at_le (xs : [u32]) (i : usize) : unit
  requires i < len xs && i < max u32 + 1
  ensures xs.[i] <= sum xs (i + 1)
= ()

A longer prefix has a larger sum.

let lemma mono (xs : [u32]) (m : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires m <= n && n <= len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  ensures sum xs m <= sum xs n
  decreases n
= if n > m then mono xs m (n - 1)

Each element is at most the sum, so a bound on the total bounds every cell. This is what proves that no cell overflows when mass arrives.

let lemma elt_le (xs : [u32]) (i : usize) (n : usize) : unit
  requires i < n && n <= len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  ensures xs.[i] <= sum xs n
= at_le xs i; mono xs (i + 1) n

An all-zero prefix sums to zero.

let lemma zero (xs : [u32]) (n : usize) : unit
  requires n <= len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. n). xs.[k] = 0
  ensures sum xs n = 0
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then (zero xs (n - 1); assert xs.[n - 1] = 0)

set is a write whose contract is the point update for the whole buffer. The element is loaded before it is overwritten: the load is what tells the solver that old (xs.[i]) is a u32.

let set (xs : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (i : usize) (v : u32) : unit
  requires i < len xs && len xs <= max u32 + 1
  ensures xs.[i] = v
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len xs). k <> i ==> xs.[k] = old (xs.[k])
  ensures sum xs (len xs) + old (xs.[i]) = sum (old xs) (len xs) + v
= let w = xs.[i] in
  xs.[i] <- v;
  update (old xs) xs i (len xs);
  assert w = old (xs.[i])

let cell = type { bed : u32; load : u32 }

The water erodes when it carries less than its capacity, at most the whole bed, and deposits the excess otherwise. Mass moves between bed and load and none is created.

let erode_or_deposit (inflow : u32) (capacity : u32) (bed : u32) : cell
  requires bed + inflow <= max u32
  ensures result.bed + result.load = bed + inflow
  ensures inflow < capacity ==> result.bed <= bed && inflow <= result.load && result.load <= capacity
  ensures capacity <= inflow ==> bed <= result.bed && result.load = capacity
= if inflow < capacity then
    (let room = capacity - inflow in
     let e = if room < bed then room else bed in
     { bed = bed - e; load = inflow + e })
  else { bed = bed + (inflow - capacity); load = capacity }

push moves the load of cell a into the inflow of cell b, downhill.

let push (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (a : usize) (b : usize) : unit
  requires a < len load && b < len inflow && len load <= max u32 + 1 && len inflow <= max u32 + 1
  requires sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) <= max u32
  ensures load.[a] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> a ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) = sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow)
= let m = load.[a] in
  let w = inflow.[b] in
  elt_le load a (len load);
  elt_le inflow b (len inflow);
  set load a 0;
  set inflow b (w + m)

drain: the load of an outlet leaves the map.

let drain (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (a : usize) (gone : u64) : u64
  requires a < len load && len load <= max u32 + 1
  requires sum load (len load) + gone <= max u32
  ensures load.[a] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> a ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures sum load (len load) + result = sum (old load) (len load) + gone
= let m = load.[a] in
  elt_le load a (len load);
  set load a 0;
  gone + m

The arithmetic that adds erode_cell's three writes up. On its own it is a small goal; inline, the solver times out on it among the sums.

let lemma balance (a : u64) (b : u64) (c : u64) (a0 : u64) (b0 : u64) (c0 : u64) (d : u32) (i : u32) (rb : u32) (rl : u32) : unit
  requires a + d = a0 + rb && b = b0 + rl && c + i = c0 && rb + rl = d + i
  ensures a + b + c = a0 + b0 + c0
= ()

docs.title: 2. One cell
docs.text:
erode_cell: a cell takes its inflow and erodes or deposits. Its bed and load are rewritten and its inflow is spent.

let erode_cell (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (c : usize) (capacity : u32) : unit
  requires c < len bed && c < len load && c < len inflow
  requires len bed <= max u32 + 1 && len load <= max u32 + 1 && len inflow <= max u32 + 1
  requires sum bed (len bed) + sum inflow (len inflow) <= max u32
  requires load.[c] = 0
  ensures inflow.[c] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> c ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) =
    sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow)
= let i = inflow.[c] in
  let d = bed.[c] in
  elt_le bed c (len bed);
  elt_le inflow c (len inflow);
  let r = erode_or_deposit i capacity d in
  set bed c r.bed;
  assert sum bed (len bed) + d = sum (old bed) (len bed) + r.bed;
  set load c r.load;
  assert sum load (len load) = sum (old load) (len load) + r.load;
  set inflow c 0;
  assert sum inflow (len inflow) + i = sum (old inflow) (len inflow);
  balance (sum bed (len bed)) (sum load (len load)) (sum inflow (len inflow))
    (sum (old bed) (len bed)) (sum (old load) (len load)) (sum (old inflow) (len inflow))
    d i r.bed r.load

One transfer of a step: the load of cell a goes to the cell it drains into, b, or out of the map at an outlet. The total is conserved, which is the loop invariant of the step to come (ADR 0055, step 4).

let transfer (bed : [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (a : usize) (b : usize) (outlet : bool) (gone : u64) : u64
  requires a < len load && b < len inflow
  requires len bed <= max u32 + 1 && len load <= max u32 + 1 && len inflow <= max u32 + 1
  requires sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + gone <= max u32
  ensures load.[a] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> a ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + result =
    sum bed (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow) + gone
= if outlet then drain load a gone
  else (push load inflow a b; gone)

docs.title: 3. A time step
docs.text:
The bound before transfer, from the totals around erode_cell.

let lemma chain (b : u64) (l : u64) (i : u64) (g : u64) (b1 : u64) (l1 : u64) (i1 : u64) : unit
  requires b + l + i + g <= max u32 && b1 + l1 + i1 = b + l + i
  ensures b1 + l1 + i1 + g <= max u32
= ()

The transport capacity of the water leaving a cell grows with its flow and with the drop to the cell below: a sixteenth of the flow plus four times the drop, at most max u16 units. It is shifts and adds, so the proof stays linear, and the shifts spread capacities over a range wide enough that the picture's colour ramp, over the number of bits of the load, shows the difference between a brook and a river.

let capacity_of (a : u32) (drop : u16) : u32 =
  let d : u32 = drop in
  let c : u64 = (a >> 4) + (d << 2) in
  if c < max u16 then c else max u16

One cell of a step: erode or deposit, record the load leaving the cell in flux for the picture, and carry it on.

let visit (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (flux : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (c : usize) (d : usize) (capacity : u32) (gone : u64) : u64
  requires c < len bed && c < len load && c < len inflow && d < len inflow && c < len flux
  requires len bed <= max u32 + 1 && len load <= max u32 + 1 && len inflow <= max u32 + 1
  requires load.[c] = 0
  requires sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + gone <= max u32
  ensures load.[c] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> c ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k])
  ensures sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + result =
    sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow) + gone
= erode_cell bed load inflow c capacity;
  chain (sum (old bed) (len bed)) (sum (old load) (len load)) (sum (old inflow) (len inflow)) gone
    (sum bed (len bed)) (sum load (len load)) (sum inflow (len inflow));
  flux.[c] <- load.[c];
  let r = transfer bed load inflow c d (d = c) gone in
  r

One time step over the map, highest cells first.

let transport (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (order : [usize]) (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (flux : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (gone : u64) : u64
  requires len down = len fill && len order = len fill && len acc = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len load = len fill && len inflow = len fill && len flux = len fill
  requires len fill <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down).
             down.[k] = k || (down.[k] < len fill && fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len fill
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len load). load.[k] = 0
  requires sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + gone <= max u32
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). load.[k] = 0
  ensures sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + result =
    sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow) + gone
=
  let g : mutable u64 = gone in
  for p in 0 .. len order
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. len load). load.[k] = 0
    invariant sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + g =
      sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow) + gone
  do
    let c = order.[p] in
    let d = down.[c] in
    let drop : u16 = if d = c then 0 else fill.[c] - fill.[d] in
    g <- visit bed load inflow flux c d (capacity_of acc.[c] drop) g
  done;
  g

The sum of a buffer, computed: what the precondition of the steps states, checked at run time.

let total (xs : [u32]) : u64
  requires len xs <= max u32 + 1
  ensures result = sum xs (len xs)
=
  let t : mutable u64 = 0 in
  for i in 0 .. len xs
    invariant t = sum xs i
  do
    t <- t + xs.[i]
  done;
  t

docs.title: 4. The height order
docs.text:
A step visits the cells from highest to lowest. height_order sorts them by filled height with a counting sort over the max u16 + 1 heights, in time O(n + max u16 + 1). It writes order, the cells from highest to lowest, and pos, its inverse, and proves that order is a permutation, each cell exactly once, and that height never increases along it. cnt, first, next, last and owner are scratch the caller passes, since Pia cannot allocate yet.

The proof has a shape worth noting. Each height gets a bucket of places in order. Placing a cell needs its bucket's next place to be free, which needs the buckets not to overlap; said directly, that compares every pair of buckets, and the solver does not settle it (#336). So owners writes, for every place, the height whose bucket holds it. A place has one owner, so buckets cannot overlap, and no goal compares two of them.

How many of fill.[k ..] have height h.

let spec count_from (fill : [u16]) (h : usize) (k : usize) : usize
  requires k <= len fill
  ensures result <= len fill - k
  decreases len fill - k
= if k = len fill then 0 else (if fill.[k] = h then 1 else 0) + count_from fill h (k + 1)

cnt.[h] is the number of cells of height h, and cnt sums to n.

let histogram (fill : [u16]) (cnt : out mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len fill <= max u32
  ensures forall (h in 0 .. 65'536). cnt.[h] = count_from fill h 0
  ensures sum cnt (max u16 + 1) = len fill
= for h in 0 .. 65'536
    invariant forall (j in 0 .. h). cnt.[j] = 0
  do cnt.[h] <- 0 done;
  zero cnt (max u16 + 1);
  for k in 0 .. len fill
    invariant sum cnt (max u16 + 1) = k
    invariant forall (h in 0 .. 65'536). cnt.[h] + count_from fill h k = count_from fill h 0
  do
    let h : usize = fill.[k] in
    let c = cnt.[h] in
    elt_le cnt h (max u16 + 1);
    set cnt h (c + 1)
  done

The bucket of height h is order.[first.[h] .. last.[h]], the highest heights first. The sum appears only in the running total acc; each bucket is stated by its neighbour.

let offsets (n : usize) (cnt : [u32]) (first : out mutable [usize]) (next : out mutable [usize]) (last : out mutable [usize]) : unit
  requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1
  requires sum cnt (max u16 + 1) = n
  ensures last.[0] = n && first.[max u16] = 0
  ensures forall (h in 0 .. 65'536). next.[h] = first.[h] && first.[h] + cnt.[h] = last.[h] && last.[h] <= n
  ensures forall (h in 0 .. 65'535). first.[h] = last.[h + 1]
= let acc : mutable u64 = 0 in
  for t in 0 .. 65'536
    invariant acc = sum cnt t && acc <= n
    invariant t > 0 ==> last.[0] = n
    invariant t > 0 ==> first.[t - 1] + acc = n
    invariant forall (h in 0 .. t). next.[h] = first.[h] && first.[h] + cnt.[h] = last.[h] && last.[h] <= n
    invariant forall (h in 0 .. t). h + 1 < t ==> first.[h] = last.[h + 1]
  do
    mono cnt (t + 1) (max u16 + 1);
    let c = cnt.[t] in
    last.[t] <- n - acc;
    acc <- acc + c;
    first.[t] <- n - acc;
    next.[t] <- n - acc
  done

An element of a [u16] read through a spec function, whose result type gives it its range inside quantifiers (#330).

let spec own (o : [u16]) (q : usize) : u16
  requires q < len o
= o.[q]

Writes t into owner.[lo .. hi] and nothing else.

let mark (owner : borrowed inout mutable [u16]) (lo : usize) (hi : usize) (t : u16) : unit
  requires lo <= hi && hi <= len owner
  ensures forall (j in 0 .. len owner). (lo <= j && j < hi ==> owner.[j] = t) && (j < lo || hi <= j ==> owner.[j] = old (owner.[j]))
= for q in lo .. hi
    invariant forall (j in 0 .. len owner). (lo <= j && j < q ==> owner.[j] = t) && (j < lo || q <= j ==> owner.[j] = old (owner.[j]))
  do
    owner.[q] <- t
  done

owner.[q] is the height whose bucket holds position q. Buckets are written from the highest height down to the lowest, which fills the positions from the end towards the start, so each bucket goes below all the ones before it: that is the only order fact this needs.

let owners (n : usize) (cnt : [u32]) (first : [usize]) (last : [usize]) (owner : out mutable [u16]) : unit
  requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1 && len owner = n
  requires last.[0] = n && first.[max u16] = 0
  requires forall (h in 0 .. 65'536). first.[h] + cnt.[h] = last.[h] && last.[h] <= n
  requires forall (h in 0 .. 65'535). first.[h] = last.[h + 1]
  ensures forall (q in 0 .. n). first.[own owner q] <= q && q < last.[own owner q]
  ensures forall (h in 0 .. 65'536) (q in 0 .. n). first.[h] <= q && q < last.[h] ==> own owner q = h
  ensures forall (a in 0 .. n) (b in 0 .. n). a < b ==> own owner b <= own owner a
= let w : mutable usize = n in
  for t in 0 .. 65'536
    invariant w <= n
    invariant t < max u16 + 1 ==> w = last.[t]
    invariant t = max u16 + 1 ==> w = 0
    invariant forall (h in 0 .. t). w <= first.[h]
    invariant forall (q in w .. n). own owner q < t && first.[own owner q] <= q && q < last.[own owner q]
    invariant forall (h in 0 .. t) (q in w .. n). first.[h] <= q && q < last.[h] ==> owner.[q] = h
    invariant forall (a in w .. n) (b in w .. n). a < b ==> own owner b <= own owner a
  do
    let lo = first.[t] in
    assert lo + cnt.[t] = last.[t] && lo <= w;
    let ht : u16 = t in
    mark owner lo w ht;
    w <- lo;
    if t + 1 < max u16 + 1 then assert lo = last.[t + 1] else ()
  done

Every place of order starts free, holding v.

let blank (order : out mutable [usize]) (v : usize) : unit
  ensures forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] = v
= for q in 0 .. len order
    invariant forall (j in 0 .. q). order.[j] = v
  do order.[q] <- v done

Each cell goes to the next free place in its height's bucket. A place q is taken when it is before next.[owner.[q]], and free (holding n) otherwise.

let place (fill : [u16]) (first : [usize]) (last : [usize]) (owner : [u16]) (next : borrowed inout mutable [usize]) (order : out mutable [usize]) (pos : out mutable [usize]) : unit
  requires len first = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1
  requires len owner = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill
  requires forall (h in 0 .. 65'536). next.[h] = first.[h] && first.[h] + count_from fill h 0 = last.[h] && last.[h] <= len fill
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len fill). first.[own owner q] <= q && q < last.[own owner q]
  requires forall (h in 0 .. 65'536) (q in 0 .. len fill). first.[h] <= q && q < last.[h] ==> own owner q = h
  ensures forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len pos && pos.[order.[q]] = q && fill.[order.[q]] = own owner q
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
= blank order (len fill);
  assert (forall (q in 0 .. len fill). next.[own owner q] = first.[own owner q]);
  assert (forall (q in 0 .. len fill). next.[own owner q] <= q);
  for k in 0 .. len fill
    invariant forall (h in 0 .. 65'536). first.[h] <= next.[h] && next.[h] + count_from fill h k = last.[h]
    invariant forall (q in 0 .. len fill).
      (q < next.[own owner q] ==> order.[q] < k && pos.[order.[q]] = q && fill.[order.[q]] = own owner q)
      && (next.[own owner q] <= q ==> order.[q] = len fill)
    invariant forall (j in 0 .. k). pos.[j] < len fill && order.[pos.[j]] = j
  do
    let h : usize = fill.[k] in
    let p = next.[h] in
    assert count_from fill h k = 1 + count_from fill h (k + 1);
    assert p < last.[h] && last.[h] <= len fill;
    assert own owner p = h;
    order.[p] <- k;
    pos.[k] <- p;
    next.[h] <- p + 1
  done;
  assert (forall (h in 0 .. 65'536). next.[h] = last.[h]);
  assert (forall (q in 0 .. len fill). q < next.[own owner q])

Sorted by fill, from sorted by owner and each cell's height being its place's owner.

let sorted_from_owner (fill : [u16]) (owner : [u16]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) : unit
  requires len order = len fill && len owner = len fill && len pos = len fill
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len pos && pos.[order.[q]] = q && fill.[order.[q]] = own owner q
  requires forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> own owner b <= own owner a
  ensures forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
= ()

The cells by decreasing fill, in linear time: a counting sort over the max u16 + 1 heights. order is a permutation with inverse pos, and a cell comes after every cell higher than it, the contract the selection sort had. cnt, first, next, last and owner are scratch.

let height_order (fill : [u16]) (order : out mutable [usize]) (pos : out mutable [usize])
    (cnt : out mutable [u32]) (first : out mutable [usize]) (next : out mutable [usize])
    (last : out mutable [usize]) (owner : out mutable [u16]) : unit
  requires len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len owner = len fill
  requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1
  requires len fill <= max u32
  ensures forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len pos && pos.[order.[q]] = q
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  ensures forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
= histogram fill cnt;
  offsets (len fill) cnt first next last;
  owners (len fill) cnt first last owner;
  place fill first last owner next order pos;
  sorted_from_owner fill owner order pos

docs.title: 5. The whole stage
docs.text:
sediment runs n time steps from the sediment in bed, with no load and no inflow. It sorts the cells first, so the order transport needs is proved, not assumed. The result is the mass that left the map, and the total is conserved exactly. If the total does not fit in a u32, nothing moves and the result is 2^64 - 1.

let sediment (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : [u32]) (n : u32)
    (bed : inout mutable [u32]) (load : out mutable [u32]) (inflow : out mutable [u32])
    (flux : out mutable [u32]) (order : out mutable [usize]) (pos : out mutable [usize])
    (cnt : out mutable [u32]) (first : out mutable [usize]) (next : out mutable [usize])
    (last : out mutable [usize]) (owner : out mutable [u16]) : u64
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len load = len fill && len inflow = len fill
  requires len flux = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill
  requires len owner = len fill && len fill < max u32
  requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down).
             down.[k] = k || (down.[k] < len fill && fill.[down.[k]] < fill.[k])
  ensures result = max u64 ||
    sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + result = sum (old bed) (len bed)
=
  height_order fill order pos cnt first next last owner;
  for i in 0 .. len fill
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. i). load.[k] = 0 && inflow.[k] = 0 && flux.[k] = 0
  do
    load.[i] <- 0;
    inflow.[i] <- 0;
    flux.[i] <- 0
  done;
  zero load (len load);
  zero inflow (len inflow);
  let t = total bed in
  if t > max u32 then max u64
  else
    (let g : mutable u64 = 0 in
     for s in 0 .. n
       invariant forall (k in 0 .. len load). load.[k] = 0
       invariant sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + g = sum (old bed) (len bed)
     do
       g <- transport fill down acc order bed load inflow flux g
     done;
     g)

docs.title: 6. Rain and a changing landscape
docs.text:
So far every cell gets one unit of water and the land stays put. Step 6 of ADR 0055 lets the rain vary, from step to step and across the map, and lets the sediment change the land: the ground the water sees is the rock raised by the sediment resting on it, so erosion cuts valleys down and deposition fills them. The C program runs the landscape in epochs: before each, it computes the ground with surface, fills its sinks and finds its directions with the first half's stages, and asks for a rainfall field (below); then evolve sorts the cells, accumulates the rain and moves sediment for k steps. Because the directions change between epochs, a little load and inflow may be left in flight; fold settles it into the bed first.

The conservation theorem is unchanged: evolve conserves sum bed + sum load + sum inflow + gone exactly, whatever the rain and however the land moved, because it counts mass, not heights.

Two buffers equal on a prefix have the same sum over it.

let lemma same_sum (xs : [u32]) (ys : [u32]) (n : usize) : unit
  requires n <= len xs && n <= len ys && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. n). ys.[k] = xs.[k]
  ensures sum ys n = sum xs n
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then (same_sum xs ys (n - 1); assert ys.[n - 1] = xs.[n - 1]; step xs ys n)

let spec at (xs : [usize]) (k : usize) : usize
  requires k < len xs
= xs.[k]

The arithmetic of one fold.

let lemma fold3 (b : u64) (l : u64) (i : u64) (b0 : u64) (l0 : u64) (i0 : u64) (x : u32) (y : u32) (z : u32) (b1 : u64) (l1 : u64) (i1 : u64) (t : u64) : unit
  requires b0 + l0 + i0 = t
  requires b1 + x = b0 + (x + y + z) && l1 + y = l0 && i1 + z = i0
  ensures b1 + l1 + i1 = t
= ()

Every cell's load and inflow settle into its bed, which conserves the total and leaves no water carrying anything.

let fold (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires len load = len bed && len inflow = len bed && len bed <= max u32 + 1
  requires sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) <= max u32
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). load.[k] = 0 && inflow.[k] = 0
  ensures sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) =
    sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow)
= for c in 0 .. len bed
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. c). load.[k] = 0 && inflow.[k] = 0
    invariant sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) =
      sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow)
  do
    fold_cell bed load inflow c
  done

One cell of fold.

let fold_cell (bed : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (load : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : borrowed inout mutable [u32]) (c : usize) : unit
  requires len load = len bed && len inflow = len bed && len bed <= max u32 + 1 && c < len bed
  requires sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) <= max u32
  ensures load.[c] = 0 && inflow.[c] = 0
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len load). k <> c ==> load.[k] = old (load.[k]) && inflow.[k] = old (inflow.[k])
  ensures sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) =
    sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow)
= let x = bed.[c] in
  let y = load.[c] in
  let z = inflow.[c] in
  elt_le bed c (len bed);
  elt_le load c (len load);
  elt_le inflow c (len inflow);
  set bed c (x + y + z);
  set load c 0;
  set inflow c 0;
  fold3 (sum (old bed) (len bed)) (sum (old load) (len load)) (sum (old inflow) (len inflow))
    (sum (old bed) (len bed)) (sum (old load) (len load)) (sum (old inflow) (len inflow))
    x y z (sum bed (len bed)) (sum load (len load)) (sum inflow (len inflow))
    (sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow))

pend starts as a copy of rain, and flow at zero.

let start_rain (rain : [u32]) (flow : out mutable [u32]) (pend : out mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires len flow = len rain && len pend = len rain && len rain <= max u32 + 1
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len flow). flow.[k] = 0 && pend.[k] = rain.[k]
  ensures sum pend (len pend) = sum rain (len rain)
= for i in 0 .. len rain
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. i). flow.[k] = 0 && pend.[k] = rain.[k]
  do
    flow.[i] <- 0;
    pend.[i] <- rain.[i]
  done;
  same_sum rain pend (len rain)

The flow through every cell under the rainfall field rain: one pass over the height order, each cell's pending water becoming its flow and moving on to the cell below. Every cell's flow is at least its own rain and at most the total rain.

let accumulate_rain (down : [usize]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (rain : [u32]) (flow : out mutable [u32]) (pend : out mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires len order = len down && len pos = len down && len rain = len down
  requires len flow = len down && len pend = len down && len down <= max u32 + 1
  requires sum rain (len rain) <= max u32
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len down). down.[k] < len down
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len pos && pos.[order.[q]] = q
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len flow). rain.[k] <= flow.[k] && flow.[k] <= sum rain (len rain)
= start_rain rain flow pend;
  let gone : mutable u64 = 0 in
  for p in 0 .. len order
    invariant sum pend (len pend) + gone = sum rain (len rain)
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. len flow). flow.[k] <= sum rain (len rain)
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. len pend). p <= at pos k ==> rain.[k] <= pend.[k]
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. len flow). p <= at pos k || rain.[k] <= flow.[k]
  do
    let c = order.[p] in
    let v = pend.[c] in
    elt_le pend c (len pend);
    flow.[c] <- v;
    set pend c 0;
    let d = down.[c] in
    if d <> c then
      (let w = pend.[d] in
       elt_le pend d (len pend);
       set pend d (w + v))
    else gone <- gone + v
  done

The terrain the water sees: the rock, raised by the sediment resting on it, a height unit per 64 units of bed, at most max u16.

let surface (rock : [u16]) (bed : [u32]) (height : out mutable [u16]) : unit
= for c in 0 .. len rock
  do
    let r : u64 = rock.[c] in
    let h : u64 = r + (bed.[c] >> 6) in
    height.[c] <- (if h < max u16 then h else max u16)
  done

One epoch of terrain evolution: k time steps under the rainfall field rain, over the terrain whose filled heights and directions the caller computed from surface. The cells are sorted by height, the flow is accumulated from the rain, every cell's load and inflow from the last epoch settle into its bed, and then the water moves sediment for k steps. The total sum bed + sum load + sum inflow + gone is conserved exactly; if the total rain or the total sediment does not fit in a u32, nothing moves and the result is 2^64 - 1.

let evolve (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (rain : [u32]) (k : u32)
    (bed : inout mutable [u32]) (load : inout mutable [u32]) (inflow : inout mutable [u32])
    (flux : out mutable [u32]) (flow : out mutable [u32]) (pend : out mutable [u32])
    (order : out mutable [usize]) (pos : out mutable [usize])
    (cnt : out mutable [u32]) (first : out mutable [usize]) (next : out mutable [usize])
    (last : out mutable [usize]) (owner : out mutable [u16]) : u64
  requires len down = len fill && len rain = len fill
  requires len bed = len fill && len load = len fill && len inflow = len fill
  requires len flux = len fill && len flow = len fill && len pend = len fill
  requires len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len owner = len fill
  requires len fill < max u32
  requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1
  requires forall (j in 0 .. len down).
             down.[j] = j || (down.[j] < len fill && fill.[down.[j]] < fill.[j])
  ensures result = max u64 ||
    sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + result =
      sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow)
=
  height_order fill order pos cnt first next last owner;
  for i in 0 .. len fill
    invariant forall (j in 0 .. i). flux.[j] = 0
  do flux.[i] <- 0 done;
  let r = total rain in
  let tb = total bed in
  let tl = total load in
  let ti = total inflow in
  if r > max u32 || tb > max u32 || tl > max u32 || ti > max u32
     || tb + tl + ti > max u32 then max u64
  else
    (accumulate_rain down order pos rain flow pend;
     fold bed load inflow;
     let g : mutable u64 = 0 in
     for s in 0 .. k
       invariant forall (j in 0 .. len load). load.[j] = 0
       invariant sum bed (len bed) + sum load (len load) + sum inflow (len inflow) + g =
         sum (old bed) (len bed) + sum (old load) (len load) + sum (old inflow) (len inflow)
     do
       g <- transport fill down flow order bed load inflow flux g
     done;
     g)

docs.title: Rainfall fields
docs.text:
The C program asks for the rain of each epoch from these. Each cell gets at most max u8 units, and a map has at most 16'777'215 cells (a 4096 by 4096 map less one cell), so the total rain is at most max u8 times 16'777'215, which fits in a u32: each field's postcondition says so, which is exactly what evolve checks before it moves anything, so with these fields its guard never trips.

A prefix whose cells hold at most max u8 sums to at most 256 per cell.

let lemma sum_le (xs : [u32]) (n : usize) : unit
  requires n <= len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. n). xs.[k] <= max u8
  ensures sum xs n <= n << 8
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then (sum_le xs (n - 1); assert xs.[n - 1] <= max u8)

The same rain r on every cell.

let rain_uniform (r : u8) (rain : out mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires len rain <= 16'777'215
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len rain). rain.[k] = r
  ensures sum rain (len rain) <= max u32
= for i in 0 .. len rain
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. i). rain.[k] = r
  do rain.[i] <- r done;
  sum_le rain (len rain)

A storm: the rows lo up to hi of a map w cells wide get inside, the others outside.

let rain_band (w : usize) (lo : usize) (hi : usize) (inside : u8) (outside : u8) (rain : out mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires w > 0 && len rain <= 16'777'215
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len rain). rain.[k] = inside || rain.[k] = outside
  ensures sum rain (len rain) <= max u32
=
  let row : mutable usize = 0 in
  let col : mutable usize = 0 in
  for i in 0 .. len rain
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. i). rain.[k] = inside || rain.[k] = outside
    invariant col < w && row <= i
  do
    rain.[i] <- (if lo <= row && row < hi then inside else outside);
    if col + 1 = w then (col <- 0; row <- row + 1) else col <- col + 1
  done;
  assert (forall (k in 0 .. len rain). rain.[k] <= max u8);
  sum_le rain (len rain)

A season: rain r everywhere when wet, none when dry.

let rain_season (wet : bool) (r : u8) (rain : out mutable [u32]) : unit
  requires len rain <= 16'777'215
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len rain). rain.[k] = (if wet then r else 0)
  ensures sum rain (len rain) <= max u32
= rain_uniform (if wet then r else 0) rain

docs.title: 7. Watersheds in linear time
docs.text:
Each epoch's picture colours every cell by its watershed and draws the streams, which needs the flow accumulation, counted in cells, and the outlet of every cell. The first half's accumulate follows a drop from every cell, which costs the total length of all the paths. The height order gives both in one pass each: the counts going down the order, as accumulate_rain does with one unit of rain per cell, and the outlets going up it, since a cell's downstream neighbour is lower and so already labelled. That a neighbour comes later in the order is the lemma later: it is strictly lower, and height never increases along the order.

An all-one prefix sums to its length.

let lemma ones (xs : [u32]) (n : usize) : unit
  requires n <= len xs && n <= max u32 + 1
  requires forall (k in 0 .. n). xs.[k] = 1
  ensures sum xs n = n
  decreases n
= if n > 0 then (ones xs (n - 1); assert xs.[n - 1] = 1)

In the height order a cell's downstream neighbour comes after it: it is strictly lower, and height never increases along the order.

let lemma later (fill : [u16]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (c : usize) (d : usize) : unit
  requires len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && c < len fill && d < len fill
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len pos && pos.[order.[q]] = q
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
  requires fill.[d] < fill.[c]
  ensures pos.[c] < pos.[d]
= let a = pos.[c] in
  let b = pos.[d] in
  assert order.[a] = c && order.[b] = d;
  assert b < a ==> fill.[order.[a]] <= fill.[order.[b]]

Every cell's watershed: the outlet its water reaches. The cells are taken from lowest to highest, so a cell's downstream neighbour, lower than it, already has its label, and the cell takes the same one.

let label_outlets (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (order : [usize]) (pos : [usize]) (basin : out mutable [usize]) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len basin = len fill
  requires forall (j in 0 .. len down).
             down.[j] = j || (down.[j] < len fill && fill.[down.[j]] < fill.[j])
  requires forall (q in 0 .. len order). order.[q] < len pos && pos.[order.[q]] = q
  requires forall (k in 0 .. len pos). pos.[k] < len order && order.[pos.[k]] = k
  requires forall (a in 0 .. len order) (b in 0 .. len order). a < b ==> fill.[order.[b]] <= fill.[order.[a]]
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len basin). basin.[k] < len fill && down.[basin.[k]] = basin.[k]
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len basin). basin.[at down k] = basin.[k]
= let n = len fill in
  for t in 0 .. n
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. len basin). n - t <= at pos k ==> basin.[k] < n && down.[basin.[k]] = basin.[k]
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. len basin). n - t <= at pos k ==> basin.[at down k] = basin.[k]
  do
    let p = n - 1 - t in
    let c = order.[p] in
    let d = down.[c] in
    if d = c then basin.[c] <- c
    else
      (later fill order pos c d;
       basin.[c] <- basin.[d])
  done

The flow accumulation and the watersheds in one linear pass each, over the height order: acc.[k] counts the cells whose water passes through k, and basin.[k] is the outlet k drains to. It gives what the first half's walk-based accumulate gives, in time O(n) rather than the total length of all the paths. rain and pend are scratch.

let drainage (fill : [u16]) (down : [usize]) (acc : out mutable [u32]) (basin : out mutable [usize])
    (rain : out mutable [u32]) (pend : out mutable [u32])
    (order : out mutable [usize]) (pos : out mutable [usize])
    (cnt : out mutable [u32]) (first : out mutable [usize]) (next : out mutable [usize])
    (last : out mutable [usize]) (owner : out mutable [u16]) : unit
  requires len down = len fill && len acc = len fill && len basin = len fill
  requires len rain = len fill && len pend = len fill
  requires len order = len fill && len pos = len fill && len owner = len fill
  requires len fill < max u32
  requires len cnt = max u16 + 1 && len first = max u16 + 1 && len next = max u16 + 1 && len last = max u16 + 1
  requires forall (j in 0 .. len down).
             down.[j] = j || (down.[j] < len fill && fill.[down.[j]] < fill.[j])
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len acc). 1 <= acc.[k] && acc.[k] <= len fill
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len basin). basin.[k] < len fill && down.[basin.[k]] = basin.[k]
  ensures forall (k in 0 .. len basin). basin.[at down k] = basin.[k]
=
  height_order fill order pos cnt first next last owner;
  for i in 0 .. len rain
    invariant forall (k in 0 .. i). rain.[k] = 1
  do rain.[i] <- 1 done;
  ones rain (len rain);
  accumulate_rain down order pos rain acc pend;
  label_outlets fill down order pos basin

docs.title: What is proved
docs.text:
Every goal in this file is proved before piac generates code:

Goal Where Every slice index is in bounds, no arithmetic overflows every function A write changes a sum by the new value less the old update, set Erosion and deposition create no mass, and erosion takes at most the bed erode_or_deposit The height order is a permutation of the cells, with its exact inverse, and height never increases along it histogram up to height_order Sediment transport conserves the total mass exactly push and drain up to transport, sediment and evolve Settling the water's load into the bed conserves the total fold_cell, fold The flow through every cell is at least its own rain and at most the total rain accumulate_rain Every rainfall field gives each cell at most max u8 units, and its total fits in a u32 rain_uniform, rain_band, rain_season A cell's downstream neighbour comes later in the height order later A cell and the cell it drains to have the same watershed, so a basin's water stays in it label_outlets Accumulation is between 1 and the number of cells, and every watershed label is an outlet, in linear time label_outlets, drainage No sediment buffer overflows the total is at most 2^32 - 1, and elt_le bounds each cell by it

What is not proved: that the capacity rule and the height of a unit of sediment are physical, and that a step carries all sediment to an outlet (it does when the order is topological, which the height order is, but the proof does not use it).

docs.title: Status and roadmap
docs.text: Pia is an experimental language under active development. The compiler proves and compiles a growing part of the language, and the rest is designed but not built. The feature index lists every built feature with a proved example, and the standard library every module written with them. Nothing is stable yet: syntax, flags and the compiled ABI can all change before a 0.1 release.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Loops need invariants. After a loop, only its invariant is known, so a goal after the loop that depends on what it did needs an invariant that says so.
  • Termination is checked for loops and direct recursion only. A while loop or a recursive call without decreases is a skipped goal, which piac refuses unless --allow-unproved accepts it. Mutual recursion is not checked.
  • Calls inside contracts to functions other than spec functions and pure functions of scalars are unknown values, so a contract cannot rely on what such a function computes.
  • Counterexamples do not show array contents yet, only lengths and scalar values.
  • Function values are partly compiled. Typed lambdas without captures, and top-level functions, can be passed to a parameter of function type, which may carry a contract, and a lambda can be bound by a let and applied (ADR 0044, steps 1 and 2). So can function objects, any record or variant with an apply, which g x calls. Function is a standard concept, and an overload set may mix functions that take values with functions that take functions. Lambdas list their captures, each copied, borrowed or referenced (inout), with loans checked to the lambda's last use (step 3). Untyped lambdas take their parameter types from where they are passed, and a let of an untyped or explicitly generic lambda is generic (step 4). Each call with a function argument is proved and compiled as its own specialisation. Partial application (add 1), functions as results (: u8 -> u8) and moved captures work too (step 7). A let of a function type holds a reference to a top-level function, proved against the arrow's contract once, with calls through it seeing only that contract (ADR 0071, step 1). A mutable reference of scalars can be rebound with <-, and a call through it compiles to an indirect call. Generic lambdas that capture, and functions stored in data, come later.
  • Floats are bit patterns to the prover with exact IEEE order, until ADR 0038's real-valued encoding lands: a goal that needs what + or * computes fails rather than being proved (verifier.md).
  • Not compiled yet: functions stored in data and generic lambdas that capture, dyn, vec<T, k>, refinement types and where on values, nested modules, and the concurrency runtime beyond spread. piac reports these as "not supported yet" at their source location.
  • Two targets, one GPU. Code generation targets arm64 macOS and x86_64 Linux; @place(gpu) runs only on Apple GPUs, through Metal.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
The plan is a sequence of milestones, each a GitHub issue, building towards the flagship demo: stream delineation and sediment transport over a terrain heightmap, proved correct and running across the CPU and GPU (ADR 0016).

Milestone Scope M0 to M7 Bazel build, grammar, parser, MLIR dialects, IRGen, verifier, arm64 codegen, records and the metaprogram engine done M8 Modules, explicit interface imports, proof certificates and a link check next M9 Generic types, concepts with laws, adapters and call-site deduction generic types and functions, value parameters on types (block u8 4) and functions generic over them, deduced from the arguments and shapes, (s : shape) with [4; 4] or [m; k] (ADR 0074, step 2: literal extents; ? extents come with step 3), overloading, concepts, the definition check, adapters, ranking by constraints and choosing by preconditions done (ADR 0034 complete); generic bodies proved once over their type parameters as well as at each instance (ADR 0043, step 1 of 5); ADR 0035: type-level metaprograms in types and where predicates, their totality check, and soft failure with --explain-overloads done (ADR 0035 complete) M10 Vectorisation driven by proved facts, and vec<T, k> M11 Floats: strict IEEE, and three ways to allow reassociation f32 and f64: literals, + - * /, negation, IEEE comparisons, conversions to and from integers and between widths, to_bits/from_bits, buffers and record fields of floats, C calls, strict codegen (no FMA contraction, subnormals kept); proofs see floats as bit patterns, with exact IEEE order and uninterpreted arithmetic until ADR 0038's encoding M12 Concurrency: spread, collectives, and compile-time checks that collectives match spread v0 done, on the CPU and, with @place(gpu), on the GPU; collectives next M13 PNG and GIF decoding and encoding, written in Pia GIF decoding and animated encoding, deflate and zlib done (ADR 0054); PNG next M14 The stream delineation demo delineation done, sediment transport done, its GIF animation written by Pia's own encoder 0.1.0 The first release: a small LLM, llama2.c's TinyStories, ported to Pia, proved, and running on Apple silicon with its matrix products on the GPU the tokenizer and the safetensors reader done; floats, the model and GPU matmuls next

Alongside these, a Presburger stage will decide affine goals such as aliasing and loop-carried dependence (ADR 0020). After a 0.1 release, Pia will be offered to Compiler Explorer.

docs.title: Following along
docs.text: The Architecture Decision Records record every design decision and why it was made. The compiler architecture describes the pipeline and the milestones in more detail.

docs.title: The standard library and its core
docs.text:
Status: accepted design, 2026-11-21 (ADR 0023). Nothing here is implemented yet. Code blocks show designed syntax.

For how the C++23 standard library maps onto these layers, header by header, see The C++23 standard library in Pia (ADR 0040).

This page answers one question: what is the smallest set of things the compiler has to provide, so that everything else in the standard library can be written in Pia and proved like any other Pia code?

It also covers two requirements that shape the answer:

  • The core calls POSIX directly and wraps it in strongly typed, contract-constrained Pia functions. There is no C layer between a Pia program and the operating system.
  • Multiplication must be provable. Today any * in a module widens the whole SMT encoding, and loop goals time out (below). A library full of width * height cannot live with that.

docs.title: Principle
docs.text:
A feature belongs in the core when one of these is true:
